One flag per hit-list entry: $FF at the start of the attack ($9FC3), ANDed with $D9 at each kill ($A720-$A729, $D9 set by $ABF1 from the killed monster's last hit points); copied to $D9 before the kill message is printed ($A1EA), which picks it ($ABE1).

Weapon class of the monster killed last in each hit-list entry's line ($A72E): the class of its line's weapon, or 1 when the monster had no attack left to make this round (its flag byte at line +$14 + n was 0, $A704-$A70A: plan_group_moves sets the flags only for a hostile group left without a move plan, and the members' ranged attacks come before any monster acts). Read at $A1F6: a ranged class (2-13, $0413) adds message 34 ('just as ... peel off a final shot').

Start of the game program: menu texts at game_menu_texts ($3E/$3F) and handler tables at game_menu_handler_tables ($40/$41), $91 = $FF (no map in memory, so the next enter_map loads one), menu 0 with item 0 selected and item 6 the last one shown (Use to Radio); draws the menu bar ($02E7), enters map $09 ($03B6: loads it and saves the game) and redraws the screen (redraw_view $AC8C). When $92 is non-zero (the start-up sets 1 at its $8301; the radio and Ranger Center programs clear it before they load the game) it first lets one turn pass on the spot (cmd_stay $AE21). Falls into main_loop.

Main loop of the game while it waits for the player. Each pass: the Geiger counter's clicks (while $9F, the distance in feet to the nearest radiation square in view, is not $FF; print_clock $B143 sets $FF when nobody in the party carries a Geiger counter, item 48: every fifth pass the click countdown in the operand $7E6A goes down; at 0 a click, sound $16 ($04D2), and a new countdown of 1 to $9F + 1, so the clicks come faster as the radiation gets nearer); the idle clock $B4/$B5 (after 16384 passes with no key, read_key clearing $B5 at each key, a turn passes on the spot: try_move_party $ADD1 with A = 4, random_encounter $B015, draw_view, after_move_encounter); a key: 1-7, up to the party's size, shows that member's sheet (view_member_cmd $AC6C), a member's function key ($5BA3: F1, F3, F5, F7 for members 1-4) runs Use for that member (use_by_member), any other key goes to the menu bar ($02DE); the self-destruct countdown (countdown_check); the end of the game when no character is left alive ($7ED5-$7EFC); View to another party (view_command $9B8C) when the current one has nobody conscious.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $7E69: the Geiger counter's click countdown. When it is 0, main_loop sets it to a random 1 to $9F + 1 ($7E72); every fifth pass (geiger_divider) it goes down one ($7E7F) and at 0 the counter clicks. 0 in the snapshots.

Not an entry point: $7E7E is the high byte of STA $7F17's operand. The tracer minted a subroutine symbol here from the engine's run_menu_item, whose JSR at $1C71 has its operand ($1C72/$1C73) rewritten before each menu handler is called; in the play-map snapshot that operand holds $7E7E, left by the program that ran before the game ($81FA in the entry snapshot).

End-of-game test, run on every pass of main_loop: with no character records in use ($0A = 0) the game is over at once; otherwise records 1 to $0A, every party's, are tested in turn (the record in end_test_record_op): one that is conscious ($02C3), or unconscious with condition UNC (CON -1 to -10, condition_index $0371 = 0) and its condition byte +$28 at 0, keeps the game going ($7F0C). An unconscious character with any condition bit, a worse condition or CON 0 counts as lost.

Prints game message A at column X, row Y ($23/$24), word-wrapped: falls into game_msg. Nothing calls $7F4C: a search of every part's and map's snapshot finds no JSR, JMP or address word for it.
Prints game message A word-wrapped ($0302), then game_msg_current_output: the game's usual way to print its own messages (88 calls in the game, and the order program's at its $CA26).
Prints game message A through the output already selected: points $43/$44 at the game's text block (select_game_text) and goes to print_message ($0311). Callers: game_msg_direct_at ($7F49) and $9E73.
Points $43/$44, the text block messages are taken from, at the game's own packed text block at $BF5F. Callers: game_msg_current_output and msg_nothing_special ($8DBF).

The melee of a battle round for the current party $08, run by the battle round ($B867) through the vector at $8E (set at $B890/$B894; $9F40 calls it once for each party on map $8D). Builds an initiative list at $5A00-$5AFF, a 16-bit value per two-byte slot (slot index in the operand $8239): slots $00-$EF the monsters, 60 bytes a group (three lines of ten), slot $F0 + 2n member n. A monster joins when its group stands within 15 feet of the party ($04CF below 16), is hostile (encounter record +9 bit 1 clear, $9EF6), its line's weapon class is not a ranged one ($0413), it is alive and its act flag (line +$14 + n) is set, which is cleared here: initiative 2d6 + 8 x its record byte +2 (multiplied in 8 bits, which would wrap from byte +2 = 32; the melee monster types in the map snapshots have 7 at most, map 15's Titanium Clawer and map 35's Brother Goliath). A member joins when conscious with order 2 (A)ttack; members whose weapon reaches farther fired earlier in the round, $9F77-$9F9B, and attack_done $A53A cleared their order, unless their target line was already empty ($9FB0), which leaves order 2 and brings them in here to strike nobody ($80CD-$80D0)): 2d6 + SP (+$11) + 4 x Brawling. Then the highest value acts (melee_pick_next) until none is left, and at the end every member whose order is 2 has the order and its argument cleared (the tables at ($89) and ($8B), $8082-$809D).

Operand of the LDX #imm at $7FA2: the group (0-3) melee_round is working on: the counter of the monster-group loop ($7F78, $8009), then the group of the line a member strikes ($80DD), added into the move-plan index at $80E3.

Operand of the LDX #imm at $7FA9: the monster line (0-2) melee_round is working on: the counter of the line loop ($7F9F, $7FFA), then the line a member strikes ($80DA) or the attacking monster's line ($818A); read by line_monster_byte2 ($82AB), by the attack messages ($81F5 miss, $8206 hit) and by the damage roll ($8214, monster_damage_roll). Cleared at $7F6B.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $804C: the party member melee_round is working on: the counter of the member loop (1 to party_member_count, $07; $801B), then the member whose turn it is ((slot - $F0) / 2, $80AB), or the member a monster attacks (chosen at random, $81C1).

Picks the next to act in melee_round: the initiative slot with the highest value (a later slot wins a tie, so members before monsters), its index kept in the operand $809F. None left (highest 0): clears order 2 (and its parameter) of members 1 to $07 (the party's member count) and returns. A slot from $F0 up is member (slot - $F0) / 2, who strikes 1 + Brawling/2 times at its target line (member_target_code $A535): each strike against a living line (member_target_alive $A52C) marks the target group as attacked (mark_target_attacked $ABC9) and hits when 1d100 is under melee_chance with base 60 when the target's group has a move planned this round ($F3EC + 4 x party + group not $FF), else 50; a miss prints message 35 ('<name> misses.'); a hit does weapon_damage_roll + 4 x the weapon's skill ($0227) + the DEX, ST and LK bonuses to a random living monster of the line (random_monster $AC5C, monster_takes_damage $AA90), may improve the skill (attack_skill_improve $AA35) and, for a kill, adds kill_experience ($A9E8) to the member's experience twice ($8163, $8166). A lower slot is a monster: melee_monster_attacks.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $809E: the slot index, in bytes, of the highest initiative melee_pick_next found ($8078); slot_clear empties that slot ($824A).

Operand of the LDA #imm at $80D5: a line index (12 x party + 3 x group + line): the line struck by the member whose turn it is ($80BC, member_target_code), or the line of the monster whose turn it is ($8192). melee_chance reads it ($8265) for the skill term; the hit, skill and kill code reads it ($8149-$815D).
BIT $32A9 hides LDA #$32 at $80F1: base 50 when the target's group has no move plan
the kill's experience is added a second time: melee kills give double ($A08A, $A719 add it once)

A monster's turn in melee_round: slot / 2 gives 30 x group + 10 x line + monster; $80D6 = its line index (line_index $BD9A for party $08). A living monster makes as many attacks as its record byte +2 ($82B4), each at a random conscious member (none left ends it): the member avoids it when 1d100 is under melee_chance with base 60 if the member's order is 5 (E)vade), 50 if it is 2 (A)ttack), else 40. A miss prints 'The <monster> miss(es).' ($9E52, message 31); a hit prints 'The <monster>', one of the map's two melee verbs (header +$56/+$57, show_map_msg_pair $BCE1 with A = $55) and does byte +3 d6 + the high nibble of byte +5 ($9EC2) to the member (member_takes_damage $A85B).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $81A6: the number (0-9) of the monster whose turn it is, within its line ($8183: slot / 2 mod 10).
BIT $32A9 hides LDA #$32 at $81DC: base 50 for a member with order 2 (A)ttack)
BIT $3CA9 hides LDA #$3C at $81DF: base 60 for a member with order 5 (E)vade)
Adds A to the initiative slot index, the operand $8239 of slot_store's LDY; returns the new index in A.
Stores A (low) and X (high) in the current initiative slot, $5A00 + the index in the operand $8239.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $8238: the initiative slot index in bytes ($5A00 + index): reset at $7F6E and $805A, moved on by slot_advance ($8231-$8234), read by melee_pick_next ($8075).
A/X = 4 x the current character's level in skill 1, Brawling ($0359, then $03FE).
Clears the initiative slot that has just acted ($5A00 + the index in the operand $809F, written by melee_pick_next), so it is not picked again.

Melee chance in $71/$72, which holds 0 on entry: adds the base in X:A, 4 x the current character's Brawling (brawling_times_4) and its AGL bonus (agl_bonus $A7BE), and takes off the skill term of the monster line in $80D6 (the line struck, or the attacking monster's): 4 x its record byte +2 when the line's weapon class is 1 (melee weapons), otherwise byte +2 less 5. Kept within 0 ($03E9 stops there) and 100. A monster type whose byte +2 is 0 makes it 0 whatever the rest: the term is negated in 8 bits with $FF as the high byte ($828B-$8290), so 0 becomes -256 (in the map snapshots only map 16's type 3, a ranged one, has 0). For a member's strike it is the chance to hit; for a monster's attack the member's chance to avoid it.

A = record byte +2 of the monster type of line $7FAA (the operand of LDX at $7FA9) in the encounter record at $77/$78, X = 0; $16/$17 is left on the monster's record ($9E9F, $9EEF). Used as its initiative weight, its number of attacks and the skill term of melee_chance, against a member's strike and for its own attacks.
Attacks left for the one acting in melee_round: 1 + Brawling/2 for a member ($80C7), record byte +2 for a monster ($81B4); counted down at $8169 and $8220. 0 in the snapshots.

The self-destruct countdown: when $F4F9 is set (map 20's action routine 4, at its $406B, sets it and keeps the elapsed-time count $04-$06 in $F4FA-$F4FC; that map's texts include 'ALERT! Self destruction sequence activated.') and the count has gone on by 240 or more since (24-bit difference), writes the map back ($03B9) and runs module 4 (run_action with $84), whatever map the party is on: no map number is tested. The count goes up by the map header's byte +$36 a step ($AF32-$AF72), four to a game minute on 39 of the 42 maps (the world map 16 with 4 minutes, map 20 1 with a quarter-minute; maps 38 and 39 count two a minute, map 40 eight), so on Base Cochise's maps 240 is an hour of game time, 240 steps on map 20. Called by main_loop on every pass ($7ED2); the JSR at the order part's $CAD2 is in that sector's stale copy of this program's first page ($CAA2-$CAFF) and never runs.

Handler of class 9 squares, radiation (square_class_handlers $ACF3): shows the map message at record byte 0 (when non-zero), then for every member of the party, conscious or not, that is not wearing item 41 (Rad suit) as armour ($0377): record byte 1 d6 of damage to CON (change_member_field $9082 with X = $1D, Y = $FF) and bit 0 set in its record byte +$28 (bit_masks), the condition byte. Text output is off meanwhile ($A1 = 1, $82E9-$832E), so no damage is printed. The $A0 = 1 set here (no armour roll) does not last: change_member_field replaces it with bit 0 of record byte 0 ($90AF-$90B4), here the message number, and clears it after each member ($90C3), so the armour roll in member_takes_damage ($A8B2) is skipped only on squares whose message number is odd. Then the party's square changes by the pair at record +2/+3 (alter_party_square $B105).
$A0 = 1 is overwritten at $90B4 for each member: see the entry comment
item 41, Rad suit, worn as armour protects
Operand of the LDA #imm at $830A: the member (1 to the party's member count $07) square_radiation is working on, written at $82EB and read back at $831E for the loop.

Bit masks 1, 2, 4, 8, $10, $20, $40, $80 for square_radiation; only the first is ever read (LDA $8335,Y at $8315 after an LDY #0 whose operand nothing changes), so radiation sets bit 0 of a character's byte +$28.

Handler of class 4 squares (square_class_handlers $ACF3; the engine draws them with tile record byte 1 AND $7F, $0B53): shows the map message at record byte 0 when non-zero ($BE1E), then the party's square changes by the pair at record +2/+3 (alter_party_square $B105).

Line of sight from the party's square ($57/$58) to column X, row Y: carry set when a class 11 square lies between them, clear when the way is clear (the party's own square is tested too, the end square is not). Steps one square at a time in x, y or both, choosing by the remainders $97/$9B, through $94/$93 (column, row), $96/$98 (|dx|, x steps left) and $9A/$9C (|dy|, y steps left); patches its INC/DEC opcodes at $839B/$83B4 (x) and $83AC/$83B2 (y) for the direction. Callers: $95A9, $97AD, $B6D1.
Opcode byte patched by line_of_sight ($8372): INC $94 ($E6) when the end square's column is at or right of the party's, DEC $94 ($C6) when left of it; the step in x.
Opcode byte patched by line_of_sight ($8357): INC $93 ($E6) when the end square's row is at or below the party's, DEC $93 ($C6) when above it; the step in y.
Opcode byte patched by line_of_sight ($835A) like $83AC: the y half of a diagonal step.
Opcode byte patched by line_of_sight ($8375) like $839B: the x half of a diagonal step.

Plans the monster groups' moves for a battle round (caller $B243): sets the 16 plan bytes $F3EC + 4 x party + group to $FF, then for every party on map $8D (select_party $9C17, the current party restored at the end) and each of its groups present: the group's act flags are cleared (group_flags_clear $BB38); a hostile group (encounter record +9 bit 1 clear) that is not stationary (bit 2 clear) gets a plan from its first line with monsters: direction 0-8 in bits 0-5, kind in bits 6-7: 0 a better position, 1 flees ($40), 2 closes in ($80). A melee line closes in unless already within 15 feet, and only when the square one step beyond the step's target is nearer than the group's distance, byte 3 (approach_step leaves move_column/move_row on the target and $8583-$858C steps again from there, $858F-$8596); non-animals flee instead below half their hit points (line_average_hp under half of byte +0/+1). A ranged line flees when weaker than the party (line_weaker_than_party; robots never), otherwise stays if its skill plus 15 (robots), 11 (cyborgs) or 7 reaches monster_range_target ($A780) at its distance, or moves to the free square next to it, in view, with the lowest target ($84DC), which need only differ from its present target, not be lower ($8550-$855C). A hostile group left without a plan (a stationary one included) gets its act flags set (group_flags_set $BB35).

Operand of the LDX #imm at $8402: the group (0-3) plan_group_moves is working on, the loop counter written at $83F6; read by plan_group_position, line_average_hp, group_flags_set/clear and for the plan index ($8568).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $8409: the party (0 to last_party, $0B) plan_group_moves is working on, written at $83E8.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $8478: the monster line (0-2) plan_group_moves is looking at, written at $8433; the line whose weapon and strength decide the group's plan.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $84CD: added to a ranged line's skill before the comparison with monster_range_target at its distance: 15 for robots, 11 for cyborgs, 7 for the others ($84A2).

Operand of the LDA #imm at $853B: the direction (0-8) the better-position search is trying, its loop counter ($84E7, $8540); the LDA hands it to plan_best_direction_op when that square is the best so far.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $8548: the best direction the better-position search has found ($853D), $FF for none yet ($84DE); read for the plan at $855E.
the best square's target is compared with the present one only for equality (BEQ at $855C)

Flee step for the group being planned: the step away from the party (dx, dy negated), else a sideways one; carry clear with A = its direction (0-8), carry set when no square is free. Shares approach_step's code.

Approach step for the group being planned (plan_group_position): dx, dy = -1, 0 or 1 towards the party ($57/$58) in move_dx/move_dy, then try_step; when that fails and one of them is 0, tries that one at -1 and then +1. Carry clear with A = the direction ($5BE3: 0 N, 1 S, 2 W, 3 E, 5-8 diagonals), carry set when nothing works.
BIT $FFA9 hides LDA #$FF at $85C2: step -1 when the party's coordinate is the smaller
BIT $00A9 hides LDA #$00 at $85C5: step 0 when the coordinates are equal

Operand of the LDX #imm at $85FF: which part of the step (0 x, 1 y) approach_step tries at -1 and then +1 ($85F2). Also a work byte: line_weaker_than_party's halving count ($869F-$86A8) and line_average_hp's loop offset and the line's count ($86FA-$8720).

Tries the step move_dx/move_dy from the group's square (group_position_at_ptr): diagonal if free, else the x part alone, else the y part alone (the other set to 0); square_free_for_group decides. Carry clear with A = the direction from direction_by_cell ($5BE3, index 3 x (dy + 1) + dx + 1), carry set when none is free.
Carry clear (A = 0) when a group may step onto column X, row Y: not column 0 or row 0, no party standing there (party_at_square $AFD6), on the map ($04D5) and class 0 ($0425); carry set otherwise.
X = move_column + move_dx, also stored back in move_column.
Y = move_row + move_dy, also stored back in move_row.
Points $79/$7A at the group being planned (party in the operand $840A, group in $8403, group_ptr $BBC7), then group_position_at_ptr.
move_column/move_row = bytes 0 and 1, column and row, of the group record at ($79).

Carry set when the line being planned (operand $8479) is weaker than the party: its average hit points (line_average_hp) under the party's average CON (party_average_con) divided by 2 to the power X (X = 1 for cyborgs, 2 for animals, mutants and humanoids).
$71/$72 = the CON (+$1D/+$1E) of the party's conscious members added up and divided by the party size $07 ($0410), counting the unconscious as 0.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $86D4: party_average_con's member counter (1 to the party's member count $07), written at $86C0.

$6F/$70 = the hit points of the line being planned (party $840A, group $8403, line $8479) added up over its ten monsters and divided by the encounter record's count for the line ($BAE6), so the dead count as 0.
Column of the square a group move is working on (plan_group_moves, try_step, step_x).
Row of the square a group move is working on (plan_group_moves, try_step, step_y).
Step in x of a group move, -1, 0 or +1 (approach_step, try_step).
Step in y of a group move, -1, 0 or +1 (approach_step, try_step).

Carries out the move plans (caller $B2B5): for each party 0 to last_party ($0B) and group 0-3 with a plan ($F3EC, in order) whose target square, one step in the planned direction (moving_group_target), has no party (party_at_square $AFD6) and is class 0: the group's old square becomes class 0, byte 0 ($0434 with $64 = $65 = 0), the group record gets the new column and row, and the new square takes the old square's class and byte (the encounter moves with it). Prints 'The <monster>' (the first line with monsters, $9E52, $38 its count) and the move's message (group_move_messages).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $873C: the party (0 to last_party, $0B) move_groups is working on, written at $8734.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $8741: the index (4 x party + group) move_groups reads the plans at $F3EC with, from 0 ($872F), one up per group ($87D1).
Operand of the LDX #imm at $87C9: the kind of the move, bits 6-7 of the plan ($875A), the index into group_move_messages.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $87D4: the group (0-3) move_groups is working on, written at $8739.
X, Y = the square one step from the moving group's square in the direction in the operand $87EF (step_square $AD9C, the direction through $5BEC).
Operand of the LDX #imm at $87EE: the direction of the move, bits 0-5 of the plan ($8750).
X, Y = the moving group's square, kept in the operands $87FA and $87FC.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $87F9: the moving group's column, before the move ($8764) and after it ($8795).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $87FB: the moving group's row, before the move ($876B) and after it ($8798).
Game message numbers for a group's move, by the plan's bits 6-7: 72 ' move(s) to a better position.', 74 ' run(s) away.', 75 ' run(s) at you.', and 0 for the unused kind 3.

Menu item Radio: asks 'Radio (Y/N)?' (game message 1, ask_yes_no $B90D); Y saves the game and the map (save_game_and_map), asks for disk side 1 and loads the program at track 26, logical sector 17, the radio part ($03AD); N redraws (redraw_view).
Menu item Save: asks 'Save game (Y/N)?' (game message 73); Y asks for disk side 1 and saves the game and the map (save_game_and_map); then redraws (redraw_view) either way.
Saves the game state ($02D8: $02-$0F and $F400-$FBFF to track 35 of the disk in the drive) and writes the current map back to its file ($03B9).

Handler of class 6 squares, actions and services (square_class_handlers $ACF3): runs the action numbered by record byte 0 (run_action: $80 + n a location module, below $80 the map's own code), then the party's square changes by the pair at record +1/+2 (alter_party_square $B105). Shop, doctor and library entrances reach it through an exit: see square_exit.

Runs action A of the square whose record is at ($5F): with bit 7 set, module A AND $7F is unpacked to $CA00 ($03BF) and called at $CA00; otherwise word A of the map's list 16 (header +$26; $0428 with Y = $10) is the address of a routine of the map's own, called through $12/$13 (jump_work_ptr $AC69) with $5F/$60 still on the record. When the action returns carry set, the screen is redrawn (redraw_view $AC8C). Callers: square_action and countdown_check (module 4). Module 0 is the doctor, 1 the shop, 2 the library, 3 the Ranger Center's entrance and 4 the Base Cochise ending.

Handler of class 12 squares (square_class_handlers $ACF3): shows map message record byte 0 ($031D) and changes other squares: five-byte entries from record +1 (flags, column, row, class/byte pair; flags bit 0: column and row relative to the party's square, bit 7: the last entry) applied by $042E with $AD/$AE kept around them; unless the last entry's flags have bit 6, redraws the view (draw_view $AC8F); then the party's own square changes by the pair after the last entry (alter_party_square $B105).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $88A1: the record offset of the change entry square_remote_changes is applying: 1, 6, 11, ... ($8887).
Operand of the ADC #imm at $88A7: what the entry's column is added to: the party's column ($57) for an entry with flags bit 0, 0 otherwise ($889B).
Operand of the ADC #imm at $88AE: what the entry's row is added to: the party's row ($58) or 0 ($889E).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $88D6: the flags of the last change entry ($88C8); their bit 6 skips the redraw.

Handler of class 8 squares, questions and passwords (square_class_handlers $ACF3): opens the text window ($0353) and prints map message record byte 0 AND $7F. Bit 7 set: the answer is one key (RETURN or back-arrow: no answer); clear: a typed line after '>' of up to 16 characters ($030E into $5A00; an empty or abandoned line: no answer). The answer is compared ($024F) with each answer message, record bytes from +3 (the last one with bit 7 set), each decoded to $5A80 (find_map_message $BE18, $03DA). The party's square then changes (alter_party_square $B105) by pair n of the list after the answers for answer n, by the pair after those for a wrong answer, or by the pair at +1/+2 for no answer; redraws (redraw_view) and returns $B105's carry. The BIT $C010 at $88FF reads a byte of this program and changes nothing: on an Apple II it clears the keyboard strobe.
Apple II leftover: clears the keyboard strobe there; on the C64 it reads this program's byte at $C010
Operand of the LDY #imm at $8958: where in $5A80 the next character of the answer message being decoded goes ($8952).

Operand of the LDY #imm at $897E: the record offset of the answer message being compared ($8946); then the offset of the pair list, 3 + the number of answers ($898C), to which twice the answer's index is added ($8993).
Operand of the ADC #imm at $898A: the number of answer messages in the record (from +3 to the one with bit 7 set), counted at $88E3-$88EF.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $898F: the index of the answer being compared, from 0 ($8941, $897B); equal to the number of answers when none matched.

Handler of class 10 squares, exits (square_class_handlers $ACF3): nothing (carry clear) while $02AA says the player answered N in exit_confirm. Otherwise shows the exit's message unless exit_confirm has ($022E), changes the exit square by the pair at record +4/+5 (alter_party_square $B105), keeps the party's column, row and map in its party table +$0B/+$0C/+$0D as the return point (the previous one kept in the operands $8A12, $8A19 and $89FC) and moves the party, setting the view's corner $02/$03 from the square ($0440): to map byte 3 at the column and row in bytes 1 and 2, taken relative to the party's square when byte 0 has bit 7 set, returning carry set (exit_enter_map); or, when byte 3 is $FF, back to the previous return point, returning carry clear ($8A00). run_square_action ($ACC1) acts on the party's square again while a handler returns carry set, so the square an ordinary exit arrives on is acted on at once and the one a return exit arrives on is not: that square is the return point, the square of the exit the party came in by (the party's $57/$58, stored at $89C1-$89D7), so acting on it would take that exit again. Shop, doctor and library entrances use this, all but map 15's library, a class 6 square that an exit arrives on: an asking (bit 6), relative exit to 0, 0 on its own map whose change makes the square class 6, so its service runs at once; that record's change $FD $FD trades the exit back (map 10: exit $402A, E7 00 00 0A 06 01, and service $3F6F, 81 FD FD), or, at map 21's Black Market, $0A $0A makes the square exit 10, which takes the party to (7,26) and puts the entrance back.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $89FB: the map of the party's previous return point (party table +$0D), kept at $89D2 before the new one is written; an exit to map $FF goes there.

Operand of the ADC #imm at $8A11: first the column of the previous return point (party table +$0B, $89BE), used by an exit to map $FF ($89EE); then what the exit's column byte is added to ($8A06: the party's column for a relative exit, else 0).
Operand of the ADC #imm at $8A18: first the row of the previous return point (party table +$0C, $89C8), used at $89F1; then what the exit's row byte is added to ($8A09).

Makes map A the current one ($09, enter_map $03B6, which does nothing when A is the map already in memory, $25BF-$25C1; otherwise the old map written back, but not one held under a number of $80 or more, $2856; the new one loaded; the game saved), draws the view (draw_view $AC8F), joins any other party standing on the same square (merge_parties_here $9959) and returns carry set. The BIT $C010 at $8A31 is an Apple II keyboard-strobe access left in; here it only reads a byte of the program.
Apple II leftover, as at $88FF: only reads a byte of the program

Exit question, from the move code ($AD83) for the square at column X, row Y the party is about to enter: when it is class 10 and its record byte 0 has bit 6 set, shows the exit's message (show_exit_message), asks 'Enter new location (Y/N)?' (game message 103) and returns carry set for N (the move is refused; $02AA = 1, $022E = 0, the view redrawn) or carry clear for Y ($022E = 1, so square_exit does not show the message again). Any other square: $02AA = 0, carry clear.
The player answered N to 'Enter new location (Y/N)?': redraws the view (redraw_view $AC8C), $022E = 0 and $02AA = 1 (square_exit then does nothing), carry set: the move is refused.
Shows the exit's message, the map message numbered by bits 0-5 of record byte 0 at ($5F), in the message area ($031D).

Menu item Use: opens the text window and the roster, asks 'Which player?' (game message 2, pick_member $02AE) unless the party has one member, and goes on in use_by_member; back-arrow redraws (redraw_view). use_by_member comes back to $8A92 to ask again when what to use is given up (or redraws when the party has one member).

Use for party member 1 with its first listed skill and no questions: $E6 = 1 (the A = 1 it stores is also the member), which makes use_choose take the skill at record +$80; falls into use_by_member. Nothing refers to $8A9E: a search of every part's and map's snapshot finds no JSR, JMP or address word for it, and the only other write to $E6 is the clear at $8B3B, so the $E6 branches in use_choose are not taken in play.

Use for party member A (from cmd_use and from main_loop for the member's function key; the JSR at the order part's $CACF is in that sector's stale copy of the game's first page, main_loop's JSR at $7ECF, and never runs): an incapacitated member (CON 0 or below) gets '<name> is incapacitated.' (game message 3) and a redraw; otherwise use_choose asks what to use (given up: back to cmd_use's question at $8A92) and use_on_square does it with $12 = the member. Afterwards carry clear goes to after_move ($AC72: the party's square is processed again), carry set redraws (redraw_view when A = 0, draw_view keeping the message area otherwise).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $8AB5: the member use_by_member is working for ($8AA2), handed to use_choose and, through $12, to use_on_square.

Asks member A what to use. Highlights its roster line, asks 'Use: I)tem S)kill A)ttribute?' (game message 4, keys use_kind_keys) unless $E6 is set (then the first skill). A skill comes from the skills page ($035C), and Medic (25) or Doctor (32) then asks 'Who do you want to heal?' (message 5): not the healer ('You can't heal yourself.'), not one at CON 0 ('is beyond help.'), not a conscious one ('must heal over time.'). An item comes from the item page ($0347, record offset $BB + 2 x its line), an attribute from 'Which: 1) Strength ... 7) Charisma' (offset $0E-$14). Except for healing it then asks the direction (ask_direction $B8D0; a square off the map asks again). Returns A = kind (0 skill, 1 item, 2 attribute), X = direction 0-4 or the patient's record number, Y = skill number, item offset or attribute offset, carry clear; carry set when given up. Callers: use_by_member and the U)se order ($B771).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $8B08: the member use_choose is asking ($8AD5): its roster line is highlighted (highlight_user), it may not pick itself to heal ($8B57), its items are listed ($8BB0).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $8BDD: the kind use_choose returns in A, 0 skill, 1 item, 2 attribute ($8AF5, $8B3D, $8BC1); $8AF8 dispatches on it.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $8BDF: what use_choose returns in X: the direction 0-4 ($8BD5) or, for healing, the patient's position ($8B64), turned into its record number ($8B87-$8B8C).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $8BE1: what use_choose returns in Y: the skill number ($8B2D), the item's record offset or the attribute's ($8BBE).
Redraws the roster line of the member being asked (the operand $8B09) highlighted ($02C9).
Key list for wait_listed_key at $8AF0: 'S', 'I', 'A' with bit 7 set ($D3 $C9 $C1) and the 0 that ends it; the index is the Use kind: 0 S)kill, 1 I)tem, 2 A)ttribute.

Carries out a Use: A = kind (0 skill, 1 item, 2 attribute), X = direction 0-4 (or the patient's record for healing), Y = skill number, item offset or attribute offset, $12 = the member. A non-player character (+$29 non-zero) may refuse ('<name> disobeys you.', game message 69). Medic and Doctor heal (use_heal). Anything else is tried on the square in that direction, which must be a check square, class 2 (use_target_checks): a pair there for that skill (a skill check, find_skill_check), item (find_item_check, one charge used) or attribute (an attribute check, find_attribute_check). Success shows the square's message +2 and changes it (use_succeeded); failure, or no matching pair, takes use_failed. Perception (skill 9) with no pair says 'You see nothing special.'. Returns carry clear when the square was dealt with (the caller then runs after_move), carry set with A = 0 or 1 otherwise. Callers: use_by_member ($8AC3) and the U)se order at the end of a battle round (order_use, $A3E3).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $8C00: the kind of Use given to use_on_square, 0 skill, 1 item, 2 attribute ($8BEF); also read by use_target_checks ($8DAA).

A Use succeeded on the check square (Y = the passing pair's offset): redraws out of combat, shows map message +2 ($9026), then changes the square by the passing pair's own change after the pair list when the flags have bit 3 (check_change_offset $9108), else by the pair at +4/+5. When the square changed, the party tries to step into it (try_move_party $ADD1; $C6 = 0 when it did); when it did not, the party moves there directly (move_party $ADDF). Carry clear.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $8C87: the offset of the pair that passed ($8C77), then that of the square change to apply ($8CA4); npc_refuses_skill keeps its Y here too ($8D8B-$8D92).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $8CBA: use_on_square's X ($8BF2): the direction (0-4) of the square the Use is aimed at, or the patient's record for healing.

A Use failed (A = 0) or no pair matched (A = $FF), kept in the operand $8DD0: $BD = the member who made the Use (the operand at $8CCB, written from $12 at $8BFA); with no effect (record +8 AND $7F = 0) shows use_fail_message; with one, shows map message +3 slowly (square_message_slow $9130), applies the effect to the member or, with flags bit 4, to the whole party ($9039, $90F5), and pauses ('(RETURN)', control code 6). Then the square changes by the pair at +6/+7 and, if it changed, the party tries to step into it (try_move_party $ADD1).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $8CCA: the member doing the Use, taken from $12 ($8BFA).

Healing with Medic (X = 2) or Doctor (X = 3) on the patient's record (operand $8CBB): nothing for one at CON 0 or a conscious one. The healer rolls the skill ($020A: 2d6 + its attribute + 4 x level; dice under 5 fail) against 15 + 5 x (|CON| >> X), only CON's low byte counting; failure: 'You didn't help <name>.' (game message 9); success: the patient's CON is halved, rounded down (an arithmetic shift with the sign kept: -3 becomes -2, and -1 stays -1, so it never rises above -1), '<name> is improving.' (message 10), and the healer's skill may rise ($020F). Carry set, A = 0.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $8D1E: use_on_square's Y ($8BF5): the skill number, the item's record offset or the attribute's.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $8D47: how many times the patient's |CON| is halved to give the difficulty: 2 for Medic, 3 for Doctor ($8D05).
ROR with the carry set: CON halved, rounded down, staying negative
Operand of the LDX #imm at $8D78: the healing's difficulty (|CON| halved 2 or 3 times, $8D4D), passed on to skill_improve_roll ($020F).

Refusal test of a non-player character for a skill: Y = $2C, then $8D8B: A = its record byte +$31 and npc_obey_check ($021F) on the byte at Y; carry set when it refuses. Entries $8D86 (item, +$2B) and $8D89 (attribute, +$2D) are hidden in the BIT instructions that follow.
BIT $2BA0 hides LDY #$2B at $8D86 (npc_refuses_item)
Entry hidden in the BIT $2BA0 at $8D85: refusal test for an item, Y = $2B (npc_refuses_skill's code from $8D8B).
BIT $2DA0 hides LDY #$2D at $8D89 (npc_refuses_attribute)
Entry hidden in the BIT $2DA0 at $8D88: refusal test for an attribute, Y = $2D (npc_refuses_skill's code from $8D8B).
A = the current character's record byte +$29, non-zero for a non-player character; Z set for one of the party's own Rangers.

Points ($5F) at the record of the square the Use is aimed at (use_target_square, is_checks_square): carry clear when it is a check square (class 2). Otherwise redraws out of combat and says 'You see nothing special.' (game message 38) for the Perception skill, 'Nothing happens.' (12) for anything else; carry set.

Shows game message 38, 'You see nothing special.', in the message area (show_message $0326 with the game's text block), carry set. The entries hidden in the BIT instructions after it show 61 'That doesn't seem to work.' ($8DB9) and 12 'Nothing happens.' ($8DBC) the same way.
BIT $3DA9 hides LDA #$3D at $8DB9: message 61, 'That doesn't seem to work.'
BIT $0CA9 hides LDA #$0C at $8DBC: message 12, 'Nothing happens.'

Message for a Use that failed with no effect: the square's own failure message (map message +3, $9029) when its flags have bit 1 or the check was tried and failed; 'That doesn't seem to work.' (game message 61) when no pair matched (operand $8DD0 negative).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $8DCF: how use_failed was reached ($8CC7): 0 when a check was made and failed, $FF when no pair matched.
X, Y = the square in the Use's direction (operand $8CBB) from the party (step_party_square $AD93).
Clears the message area and redraws the view (redraw_view $AC8C) unless a battle is on ($D8 non-zero: returns at once).
Prints control code 6, the '(RETURN)' pause ($0323), unless a battle is on ($D8 non-zero).

Move test for the square at column X, row Y (square_blocked's $AD7B; kept in checked_square's operands): carry clear when it is not a check square (class 2) or its checks wait until the party is on it (flags bit 7). Otherwise its checks run (square_checks), again for as long as they change the square: carry clear when they pass (A = 0), carry set when they fail or it has no checks (bit 6 clear): the move is refused.
X, Y = the square blocking_check_square is testing, kept in the operands $8E10 and $8E12 (0 as loaded; $37, $3E in the play-map snapshot).
Operand of the LDX #imm at $8E0F: the column blocking_check_square is testing ($8DEC); 0 as loaded, $37 in the play-map snapshot.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $8E11: the row blocking_check_square is testing ($8DEF); 0 as loaded, $3E in the play-map snapshot.

Handler of class 2 squares, check squares (square_class_handlers $ACF3), X, Y = the square: run for the party's own square by run_square_action ($ACC1) when the flags (record byte 0) have bit 7, otherwise for the square the party tries to enter (blocking_check_square). Shows map message +1, then, when the flags have bit 6, tests the party's conscious members against the pairs from record +$0A (two bytes each, $FF after the last; kind = first byte >> 5: 0 skill (difficulty 0: knowing it is enough), 2 attribute, 3 party size (equal to the second byte), 4 cash (passes when the member has less than the second byte, fails at once, without trying the other pairs, when the member has that much, $8E73-$8E83; the check takes no money: the maps write a purchase as the failure, whose effect takes it, as in map 2's bar, which fails a member with 10 or more and takes 10 with the effect cash - 10 at +8/+9, its success message being 'You don't have enough money.'), others an item that is carried and loses a charge; low five bits the difficulty). A member passes with the first pair it passes; one who passes none gets the effect at +8/+9 (bit 4: on everybody, which ends the tests). Bit 5: every conscious member is tested, else the first one decides; bit 2: one pass is enough. Success: message +2 and the square changes by the pair at +4/+5 (with bit 3, by the passing pair's own change, at the first pass). Failure: the pair at +6/+7 and message +3, which an effect brings with it instead: slowly for one on CON (+$1D) or on everybody, plainly for one on cash (+$15), not at all for one on another field ($8ED3-$8EE4, $8F28-$8F3C). Returns A = 0 success, 1 failure, or 1 with carry clear and nothing changed when there are no checks (bit 6 clear), with $042E's carry (set when the square changed).
carry set (cash at least the amount) fails this member at once; the failure's effect, not this check, takes the money (map 2's bar)
Operand of the LDY #imm at $8EA9: the offset of the check pair square_checks is trying ($8E49: $0A, $0C, ...).

Operand of the LDA #imm at $8ECF: how many times square_checks has applied the square's effect ($8EEC, $8F14), 0 at the start ($8E25). Only the first effect brings map message +3 (slowly for an effect on CON, field $1D, and for an effect on everybody; plainly for one on cash, $15; none for another field); when an effect was given, the failure end does not show message +3 again but pauses after an effect on CON ($8F28-$8F3C).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $8EE7: the member (1 to the party's member count $07) square_checks is testing ($8E3C), the one a failure's effect is applied to.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $8F02: the number of members who passed none of the pairs ($8EC0), 0 at the start ($8E22).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $8F24: the number of members who passed a pair ($8F46), 0 at the start ($8E1F).
Operand of the LDX #imm at $8F68: the column of the square square_checks is working on ($8E14), changed at the end.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $8F6A: the row of the square square_checks is working on ($8E17).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $8F6F: square_checks' result in A, 0 success, 1 failure ($8F3F), 0 at the start ($8E28).

Carry clear when the check square at ($5F) has its checks run once the party stands on it (flags, record byte 0, bit 7 set): the move test lets the party on and run_square_action runs them ($ACC9); carry set when they run as the party tries to enter (blocking_check_square) instead.
Carry set when the square at column X, row Y is class 2, a check square, with ($5F) on its record (square_action_record $B12D), carry clear otherwise.

Looks for an item pair (kind 1) on the check square for the item at offset Y of the current character (the item number taken from it): found, uses a charge of the item ($0380) and returns A = 0, Y = the pair's offset, carry clear; none, carry set (A = $FF).
Operand of the CMP #imm at $8FA1: the item number find_item_check is looking for ($8F89).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $8FA5: the offset of the pair find_item_check is looking at ($8F8E), returned in Y when it matches ($8FB0).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $8FAB: the record offset of the item find_item_check was given ($8F84), whose charge is used when a pair matches.

Looks for a skill pair (kind 0) on the check square for skill A: found, the current character makes the skill check ($0207 with the pair's difficulty) and the routine returns its carry (clear = passed) with Y = the pair's offset and A = 0; none, carry set with A = $FF.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $8FD3: the skill find_skill_check is looking for ($8FB9).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $8FD7: the offset of the pair find_skill_check is looking at ($8FBE), returned in Y ($8FE9).

Looks for an attribute pair (kind 2) on the check square for the attribute at record offset A: found, the current character makes the attribute check ($0212 with the pair's difficulty) and the routine returns its carry (clear = passed) with Y = the pair's offset and A = 0; none, carry set with A = $FF. The code runs on to $9025.

Inside the attribute-pair scan whose entry is $8FEF (A = the record offset of an attribute, kept at $9008): a check pair of kind 2 (check_pair_kind) whose second byte is that offset is the one; any other pair is skipped ($900B, two bytes on). The match goes to $9013: check_pair_low5 gives the difficulty and attribute_check ($0212) makes the check against that attribute; Y = the pair's offset ($900C), A = 0. No match before the $FF: carry set ($9011).

Operand of the CMP #imm at $9007, written at $8FEF (the attribute scan of a check square's pairs): the record offset of the attribute the player chose, compared with the second byte of each kind-2 pair.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $900B, written at $8FF4: the offset of the check pair the attribute scan is looking at ($0A, $0C, ...); $9020 reloads it so the scan returns Y on the matching pair.

Shows map message number record byte +2 of the square at ($5F) in the message area, if that byte is non-zero ($BE1E: show_map_message). Second entry $9029, inside the BIT at $9028, does the same with byte +3. Callers of $9026: the check-square handlers $8C7D, $8F50, $8F63.
Entry hidden in the BIT $03A0 at $9028 (LDY #$03): shows map message number record byte +3 of the square at ($5F) when it is non-zero ($BE1E). Reached from $8DD3 (JMP), $8EE4 and $8F2D.

A = the record byte at ($5F)+Y shifted right five times (the LSR here, four more at $A5FC): the kind of a check pair. The check-square code dispatches on it ($8E52): 0 skill, 2 attribute, 3 party size, 4 cash, any other value an item that must be carried and loses a charge. Y kept.
A = the record byte at ($5F)+Y AND $1F: the low five bits of a check pair's first byte, the difficulty of a skill or attribute check (for a skill, 0 means owning it is enough, $8EAE). Y kept.

Applies the check square's effect, record bytes +8 and +9 at ($5F), to party member A: nothing when +8 is 0 (the BEQ at $9046 tests the whole byte). The field is +8 AND $7F, a character-record offset. The amount is +9 AND $7F as it stands when +8 has bit 7 set, otherwise that many d6 ($BDC4); it goes to $6F/$70 ($0401). Bit 7 of +9 means subtract. Runs in slow scroll at the speed in $906A (2 at first; $907A keeps whatever speed the player set with the cursor keys for the next effect), applies it through change_member_field, then restores the scroll mode and speed (slow_scroll_restore).

Operand of the LDX #imm at $9069: the scroll speed apply_square_effect uses for its text, 2 as loaded; $907C stores the speed $0F there after each effect, so a speed the player changes with the cursor keys sticks for the next effect.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9073: the party member apply_square_effect works on, stored at $9039.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $9075: the character-record offset of the field the effect changes (record byte +8 AND $7F), stored at $904B.

Changes field X (a character-record offset) of party member A by the amount in $6F/$70; Y bit 7 set subtracts, clear adds. Subtracting: CON (+$1D) is damage, printed and applied by $A85B (amount in A/X, member in Y) with $C8 = 1 and $A0 = bit 0 of the square record's byte 0 during the call; cash (+$15) goes through spend_cash ($03CE: nothing taken when the member is short); any other field loses the low byte of the amount and stops at 0. Adding: experience (+$21) gains it through $03DD ($0825, saturating); any other field gains the low byte unless the sum passes 255, in which case it is left unchanged.

Operand of the LDY #imm at $908E: the direction byte (record byte +9 from apply_square_effect, $FF from square_radiation at $830E; bit 7 set subtracts), stored at $9088 and tested by the BPL after the load.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9092: the character-record offset of the field being changed, stored at $9082 and reloaded at $90D5.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $90BA: the party member, stored at $9085, handed to the damage routine $A85B in Y.
Applies the check square's effect (apply_square_effect) to every member of the current party in turn, 1 to $07. Used when the square record's flag byte has bit 4 set ($8CE6, $8F1A).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $90FE: the member apply_effect_to_all has just done, stored at $90F7; the loop goes on while it is below $07 (the INY at $9100 comes before the compare).

Y = the offset of the check pair that passed (+$0A, +$0C, ...): skips the pairs to their $FF terminator and returns Y = terminator + 1 + (pair - $0A), the offset of that pair's two-byte square change in the list that follows the terminator (same order, two bytes each). $0A00 then applies it. Callers: $8C89, $8F56.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9115 and check_change_offset's scratch byte: the pair offset it was given (stored at $9108), then the terminator offset + 1 (stored at $911B) added to it at $911F.
A = record byte +8 of the square at ($5F) AND $7F, the field offset of the check square's effect (0 when it has none, Z set); Y = 8.

A = record byte +0 of the square at ($5F) with Y = 0: the check square's flag byte, tested bit by bit by its handlers (bit 0 at $90B2, bit 1 at $8DCB, bit 2 at $8F20, bit 3 at $8C83 and $8F4C, bit 4 at $8CE2 and $8EC6, bit 5 at $8EF2, $8F0B and $8F5F, bit 6 at $8E33, bit 7 at $8F75). The bit 0 test is change_member_field's ($90AF), which square_radiation also reaches with a class 9 record, whose byte 0 is its message number.

Shows map message number record byte +3 of the square at ($5F) in the text window (text_window_select, print_map_message) in slow scroll at speed 2, waits four delay rounds (delay_x_times), then falls into slow_scroll_restore. Callers: $8CDC, $8EDA, $8F17.

Puts back the scroll speed $0F and the slow-scroll flag $A8 that slow_scroll_on saved into the operands of these two LDA #imm ($9145, $9149). Reached at the end of square_message_slow and by JMP from apply_square_effect ($907F).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9144: the scroll speed $0F as it was before slow_scroll_on, stored at $9154.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9148: the slow-scroll flag $A8 as it was before slow_scroll_on, stored at $914F.

Saves the slow-scroll flag $A8 and the scroll speed $0F into slow_scroll_restore's operands, then sets $A8 = 1 (text pauses line by line and the cursor keys change the speed, engine $253A) and the speed $0F = X.

The last test of a move into the square at column X, row Y ($AD8B, after the class 2 and class 10 handlers): $B12D gives its class and points ($5F) at its record. Class 11: map message +0 is shown when non-zero, and unless record byte +1 is negative the square change at +1/+2 is applied to that square ($0A00); carry set, the party stays. Class 4 (an object square, whose tile is record byte +1 AND $7F, engine $0B8E): passable, carry clear, unless +1 has bit 7 set; then the same with the change at +2/+3, carry set. Any other class: carry clear.
Entry for class 11, hidden in the BIT $01A2 at $9179 (LDX #$01): the square change is read from record offset 1. Class 4 arrives at $9177 with offset 2.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9184: the record offset of the square change bump_blocking_square applies (1 for class 11, 2 for class 4), stored at $917C.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $918B: the column of the square being moved into, stored at $915E.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $918D: the row of the square being moved into, stored at $9161.

Square class 5, a loot bag (entry 5 of the square-class table at $ACF3, run through $ACDB). ($5F) is the bag's record: +0/+1 the square change made once it is empty, then entries of an item byte and a count byte from +2 to a $FF. Each entry is fixed in the map's record the first time the bag is opened (enter_map writes the map back with it): an item byte 1-$5D with bit 7 clear names an item class and becomes a random item of that class (count_items_of_class, then the n-th match) with bit 7 set, or 0, an empty entry, when no item has that class ($91CF); $5E (Cash) becomes $DE and the two bytes after it are each rolled from 1 to themselves (a 16-bit amount, so a cash entry takes three bytes); a count with bit 7 set becomes 1 to (count AND $7F). Counts entries in $4D and non-empty ones in $4E (both from 1, for the list), $D1 past the last, then goes on at loot_pick_member.

Operand of the LDY #imm at $91CD, loot_square's offset of the entry being fixed (from +2 in steps of two, one more for a cash entry, $91C2), stored at $919E and, for the entry loot_pick_member takes, at $9258; read back at $91F2, $91FC, $920B, $92A0, $92C7.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $91E1: the item number loot_square's random pick is counting through (from 1 up), stored at $91DB and stepped at $91DE.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $91E9: the entry's item byte AND $7F, the class searched for while fixing a bag ($91B1), then the item chosen from the list ($9260).

Second half of loot_square: shows the roster, asks 'Who wants loot?' (game message 16) and takes a member (pick_member); left-arrow clears the message area ($AC8C) and returns carry clear. A member who is not conscious gets message 17 ('can't get any') and the question again. Then the bag is listed (loot_list_setup, list_show_page) and list_choose takes an entry: left-arrow asks for a member again. Cash is added to the member (cash_add) and the entry emptied, with the byte after it set to $FF so it ends the list once the entry is two bytes again; an item goes to the first free slot with its record's byte 4 as the count byte (find_free_slot; 'You can't carry any more.', message 18, and a call to play_sound_1 ($0232), whose sound record starts no note, when full) and the entry's count drops by one. When an entry empties, $4E drops; at 1 (nothing left) the square change at record +0 is made (A = 0, $B105) and its carry returned.
Y + 1, then the record byte at ($5F)+Y becomes a random number from 1 to itself (random_1_to_a; 0 stays 0). loot_square calls it twice to roll a cash amount, low byte then high byte ($91BC).

A = an item class: returns A = the number of items from $5E (Cash) down to 1 whose class is A (record from $0BCD, then item_class), Z set when none. A = 0 returns $5E at once, a value loot_square never asks for (it skips entries whose byte is 0).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $92FB: count_items_of_class's item counter, $5E stored at $92F8, stepped down to 1 at $930A.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $9303: the class count_items_of_class is looking for, stored at $92EE.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $930F: count_items_of_class's tally of matching items, cleared at $92F3, stepped at $9307, returned in A.

Starts the loot list: direct output, game message 19 ('<name>, take an item' and the '#  ITEM' heading) through $7F44, the first entry on the page $4A = 1, and the list's per-line routine $47/$48 = loot_list_line.

Per-line routine of the loot list (vector $47/$48, called by list_show_page with A = entry k): reads entry k at record offset 2k. An empty entry (item 0) returns carry set and is not shown. Otherwise prints the line's label (list_line_label), the count right-aligned in four columns (for Cash, item $5E, the 16-bit amount, print_word_padded; also kept in $38 for the plural), a space and the item's name ($0BDC: engine message item + $24); carry clear.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9345: the record offset of the entry loot_list_line is printing (2k), stored at $932F.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $934C: the item number loot_list_line is printing, stored at $9338, compared with $5E (Cash) and passed to $0BDC.

Turns the position records ($5B4F: 16 records of x, y, map, distance, four per party) into battle groups ($EE00 + $178 x party + $5E x group, group_ptr). First pass: a group whose x, y and map match a record (find_group_at_record) is swapped (swap_group_records) into the record's own place, record n belonging to party n/4, group n AND 3 (position_to_group). Second pass, for each record no group matches: with the record's party selected ($9C17), that group gets the record's x, y and map and its distance in feet ($04CF); ($77) is pointed at the encounter record of the square (group_square_record); the monster numbers and counts of its three lines (record bytes 3/4, 5/6, 7/8, tables $BAE9 and $BAE6) that have bit 7 set are rolled, 1 to the low seven bits, and written back, so they stay fixed; the encounter's message (record byte 2) is printed and the group announced (print_group_appears: counts, names, ' appear at d feet.'); and every monster of each line gets its hit points, a word each in the line's record: a quarter of the monster's 16-bit seed (monster record bytes 0/1) + 1 to the low byte + 256 x (1 to the high byte), random_1_to_a giving 0 for 0. Called at $B23D in the Enc command ($B1A3), right after scan_for_encounters. Reselects the party it started with.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9376: the offset (0-$3C, steps of 4) of the position record place_encounter_groups is working on; stored at $9373, $9383, $93BD, $93CE.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $93A4: the party of the battle group matched to the position record (find_group_at_record, stored at $939B); in the second pass, the party the record belongs to ($93EA).
Operand of the CPX #imm at $93A8: the group number to go with $93A5 (stored at $939E and $93ED).
Operand of the LDX #imm at $940F: the column of the position record's square (from $5B4F), stored at $938D and $93D9, for the distance $08F5.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9411: the row of the position record's square (from $5B50), stored at $9393 and $93DF.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $9430: the line (0-2) of the encounter record place_encounter_groups is rolling or giving hit points, stored at $941F and $9459.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9488: the high byte of the monster's hit-point seed (monster record byte 1, $9EE6), stored at $9477.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $948C: the low byte of the monster's hit-point seed (monster record byte 0), stored at $9474.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $94AB: the offset of the hit-point word being written in the line's 30-byte record (0, 2, 4, ...), stored at $9485.
A = party, X = group of the position record place_encounter_groups is on (offset $9377, through position_to_group).

Looks for encounters around every party on the battle map $8D. Entered here with A = 0 (called at $B23A and $B2BE); the entry $94CF, hidden in the BIT at $94CE, sets A = 1, which also draws on the calling party's view (called at $ACA5 and $B19B). Clears the 16 position records at $5B4F; $F4E1 + party (parties 0-3) = the longest reach among the party's members (member_reach: 0 down, 15 melee, $FE a gun with rounds). Then each party 0 to $0B on map $8D scans the squares of its 19 x 9 view ($02/$03, $54 columns, 9 rows) for class 3 or 15. Such a square counts when the party can see it (no class 11 square on the line, $8347), has a conscious member, and its distance in feet (tenths of a square, $04CF) is within the encounter record's byte 1, or within both the party's reach and byte 0. It is recorded ($97F2) for the nearest party that can engage it (encounter_party_distances, nearest_engaging_party), four records a party; when that party's four are in use the square replaces the first of them that is farther away, or goes to the next-nearest party. Moving or replacing a record ($959A) starts the scan over. The end, $9707, clears groups that lost their record. Returns carry clear when a record was made and a recorded encounter is hostile (record byte 9 bit 1 clear), carry set otherwise.

Entry hidden in the BIT $01A9 at $94CE (LDA #$01): scan_for_encounters with drawing on. On the calling party's view, an encounter square within its record's byte 0 shows the tile for the monster kind of its first line whose type byte is non-zero ($95DE-$95EA; $5BF5 + monster record byte 6; kind 3 while the monster number is still unrolled), and an encounter square it cannot see or that lies beyond byte 0 is redrawn as the map has it (redraw_scanned_square).

Operand of the LDA #imm at $9501, a counter used three ways: the member (1-$07) whose reach is being tested ($94F1-$950A), the party (3 down to 0) in encounter_party_distances ($9783-$97CF), and a position-record offset ($9691, $96A8, $971F).

Operand of the CMP #imm at $9510: the longest reach found so far among the party's members ($9514); then reused for the distance in feet from the scanning party to the square ($95C4), read at $9613 and $9627.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9525: the party that called scan_for_encounters ($94E0); compared at $95D9 and $982F, reselected at $959D.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9536: the party being scanned, 0 to $0B; stored at $9533, stepped at $958D.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $953D: the battle map $8D the scan is for ($94E5); also compared at $974D and $9799, passed at $975B.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9599: set to 1 when a position record was moved ($9824) or a farther one replaced ($96FE); the scan then starts over.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $95FD: 1 when scan_for_encounters was entered at $94CF (drawing on), 0 at $94CC; stored at $94D1, tested at $95FF and by redraw_scanned_square ($9828).

Operand of the LDA #imm at $9649: the party nearest_engaging_party chose, stored at $9652 and $96C4. On the path for a square that already has a record, $9649 loads it before this pass stores the new choice (at $9652), so the party compared with the record's holder ($964C) is the one chosen in an earlier pass, and the new record's distance ($964F into $9672) is that party's number, 0 to 3, not a distance.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $964B: the party whose four position records already hold this square (find_position_record, stored at $963C); compared again at $968C and $96A3.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $9671: the distance kept with a new position record (store_position_record puts it at +3) and compared with the party's records ($9673, $96E6); stored at $96C1 from nearest_engaging_party, and at $964F, where it is the party number loaded at $9649 (see $964A).

End of scan_for_encounters, for every party 0-3 and group 0-3: when the group's position record is in use, notes ($9777) whether the encounter on its square is hostile (record byte 9 bit 1 clear, encounter_is_peaceful); then clears the battle group (group_clear $BC67) when it is empty, or is on map $8D with no position record for its square. Returns carry clear when a record was made ($9775) and one is hostile, carry set otherwise.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9774: 1 once scan_for_encounters has stored a position record ($980B); cleared at $952B.
Operand of the AND #imm at $9776: 1 when a recorded encounter is hostile (record byte 9 bit 1 clear, $973E); cleared at $9709. With $9775 it makes the carry: clear when both are set.

For the square at $983F/$9841 and its record ($77): $F3E0+party = the distance in feet from each party 0-3 ($08F5), or $FF when the party does not exist, has nobody conscious, is on another map than $953E, has the square outside its view ($B119), cannot see it ($8347), or is farther than the record's byte 1 and its own reach ($F4E1+party). Reselects the party it started with.
Picks the smallest of $F3E0+party for parties 0 to $0B: A = that distance and X = the party; A = $FF (and X = 0) when every entry is $FF.
Fills position record Y ($5B4F+Y): column $983F, row $9841, map $09 and the distance $9672; sets the found flag $9775.
Clears the position record of the square at $983F/$9841 on map $09 (find_position_record) and asks for the scan to start over ($959A = 1).

Called for an encounter square the scanning party cannot see ($95AE) or that lies beyond its record's byte 0 ($95CF). With drawing on ($95FE) and the calling party scanning: redraws the square as the map has it (draw_square, $04DB) and returns carry clear. With drawing on and another party scanning: carry set, so that party passes over squares beyond byte 0. With drawing off: carry clear, and the range checks go on.
X = the column, Y = the row of the square the encounter scan is on (the operands at $983F and $9841, stored at $955D and $9548).
Operand of the LDX #imm at $983E: the column of the square being scanned.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9840: the row of the square being scanned.

A = map, X = column, Y = row: looks through the 16 position records at $5B4F for one with that square (an x of 0 marks a free record and never matches): carry set, A = its party (record number / 4) and Y = its offset when found; carry clear when not.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $9855: the column find_position_record looks for.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $985C: the row find_position_record looks for.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $9863: the map find_position_record looks for.

Y = a position record's offset: searches the battle groups of every party 0-3, groups 0-3 ($BBC7), for one whose x, y and map (+0, +1, +2) match the record: carry set with A = party and X = group when found, carry clear when not.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $9887: the position-record offset find_group_at_record compares with, stored at $9877.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $98A2: the party find_group_at_record is on (0-3), returned in A.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $98A4: the group find_group_at_record is on (0-3), returned in X.
A = party: Y = the offset of its four position records, from party_record_offsets (0, $10, $20, $30).
Four bytes 0, $10, $20, $30: the offset of each party's block of four position records at $5B4F, read by party_record_block.
A = a position-record offset (0-$3C): returns A = the party (offset / 16) and X = the group (offset / 4 AND 3) whose battle group the record belongs to.
Swaps the $5E-byte battle group of party A, group X ($BBC7, kept in $12/$13) with the group belonging to position record Y ($98C5), byte by byte.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $98DD: the position-record offset given to swap_group_records in Y, stored at $98CF.

A = a character record, X = column, Y = row: moves that character to the square in a party of its own, split off as party $0B + 1 (copy_member_to_party, then remove_record_from_party, $0B raised), unless it is alone in its party or there are four parties already, in which case its whole party moves there. Nothing for a character whose CON (+$1D/$1E) is 0 or below. Leaves that party current, its new square stored in its table ($9C17 twice). Called by resolve_runs_and_moves ($A306) for each runner, with the square from square_blocked ($AD5B).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9907: the runner's character record (A at entry, stored at $98F5).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $991D: the runner's party (find_party_of, stored at $9901); after a split the new party, $0B ($9941).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9926: the runner's position in its party, the Y that find_party_of leaves (stored at $9904).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $994A: the column the runner goes to (X at entry, stored at $98F8), put in $57.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $994E: the row the runner goes to (Y at entry, stored at $98FB), put in $58.

Merges into the current party one other party standing on the same square (map $09, column $57, row $58, from its table's +10, +8, +9), searching from party $0B down: copies its members in (copy_member_to_party, $07 raised for each), closes up the party tables over it (each later 14-byte table moves down one), lowers $0B and clears table 3 (clear_party_table). The current party number $08 drops by one when it came after the merged party, and $B6 drops when it is at or above both. Carry clear when a party was merged; carry set when none was found ($9969). Called after each battle round for every party ($B8B4), after a move ($AC7B), after an exit ($8A2E), for a runner ($A30C) and after a party's move order ($A364).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $995E: the party compared with the current one, from $0B down to 0 (stored at $995B); then the party being merged, and the table being closed up ($99B8-$99DE).
Points $68/$69 at the current party's table (party_table_ptr) and returns carry set: merge_parties_here's way out when no party shares the square, and its tail after a merge ($99E9, then CLC).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $999D: the position (1 up) of the member of the merged party being copied in, stored at $998D.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $99C8: the source offset as the party tables are closed up, $1B down to $0E (the next table's bytes), stored at $99C0.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $99CC: the destination offset, $0D down to 0, stored at $99C5.

D)isband (command table word at $7F1E): nothing for a party of one. With four parties already, 'No more can disband.' (message 21). Otherwise 'Who wants to disband?' (22), then member keys 1 to $07 until RETURN, back-arrow, or all members but one chosen. A chosen member goes to the new party $0B + 1 with its name printed (copy_member_to_party), or ' has been chosen.' (23) when it is already there. A member whose CON is below 0 gets ' is unconscious.' (24) and stays; one whose CON is exactly 0 (dead) is offered 'Do you want to bury {0B}?' (79, 78); an NPC (+$29 non-zero) is first offered 'Do you want to dismiss {0B} forever?' (79, 77) when two or more characters are conscious. Y to either removes the character for good (remove_member) and ends the command. When members were chosen: 'Which way?' (ask_direction), they leave the old party (remove_record_from_party), the new party becomes current (view_party) and steps that way (try_move_party $ADD1), then $AC72. Back-arrow at any prompt clears the new party's table and returns.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9A0D: the record being counted ($99FF, 1 to $0A), then the member chosen (1 to $07, $9A59), then the position of the new party being moved out of the old one ($9AD8).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9A65: the number of conscious characters in all records, counted at $99FD-$9A16; an NPC is offered dismissal only when it is 2 or more.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9AA0: the number of the new party, $0B + 1 (stored at $9A33), into which chosen members are copied; its table is cleared on back-arrow ($9AAF).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9ABE: how many members have been chosen, cleared at $9A2B, counted at $9AB8; choosing stops when it is one less than the party's size, and nothing happens when it is 0.

A = a position (1-7) in party X, Y = another party: adds the record at that position to party Y's table (party_add, $07 put back), gives party Y the current party's square and map ($57, $58, $09: save_party_position) and party X's table bytes +11 to +13. Carry clear with A = the record; carry set when the position is empty or party Y holds the record already. Party X keeps the record: the caller takes it out.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9B43: the party copy_member_to_party adds the member to (Y at entry, stored at $9B27).

Three bytes where copy_member_to_party keeps bytes +13, +12 and +11 of the source party's table ($9B3C) while it switches tables, then writes them to the destination's +13 to +11 ($9B5D). Bytes +11 to +13 are the return point of the last exit, its column, row and map: square_exit writes them ($89BA-$89D7), and an exit whose byte +3 is $FF reads them back ($89EE-$89FC). Work space, 0 in the snapshots.

A = a character record: takes it out of the current party's table, moving the later positions up one and clearing position 7, and lowers $07. The record must be in the table: when it is not, party_has_record leaves Y = 8 and the loop runs Y round from 9 through 255 and 0 to 7, moving the 256 bytes from the table on down one. Callers: runner_split_off ($993A) and disband_command ($9AE5), both with a record known to be there.

V)iew (command table word at $7F20; also called at $7F11 when the current party has nobody conscious): selects the next party, $08 + 1 wrapping after $0B to 0, that view_party accepts, then goes on at $AC89 (the encounter check $B197). When the search comes round to the party it started from, the clock moves on (advance_clock $AF32, shown by $B143) and that party is taken again: with one party, V)iew lets time pass.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9B94: the party view_command tries next (stored at $9B9E), stepping on from the current one and wrapping to 0 after $0B through the LDY #$00 hidden at $9B9C.
Entry hidden in the BIT $00A0 at $9B9B (LDY #$00): the party after the last one ($0B) is party 0.
Operand of the CPY #imm at $9BA1: the party current when V)iew began (stored at $9B91); when the search reaches it again the clock moves on and it is selected again ($9BAE).

A = a party: makes it current ($9C17) when it has a conscious member; if its map differs from the one in use, 'They aren't on this map. Are you sure you want to view them (Y/N)?' (message 27) and enter_map on Y. Then $AC8C and carry clear. Otherwise the party that was current is selected again and carry set: after N; or, when the party has nobody conscious, after 'You can't view this party.' (message 14) if another party exists and some record 1 to $0A is conscious. Callers: view_command, disband_command ($9AF3).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9BDD: the character record (1 to $0A) view_party tests for anyone conscious, stored at $9BD2.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9C10: the party current when view_party was entered (stored at $9BC0), selected again when it fails.

A = a party (0-3): stores the current party's square and map ($57, $58, $09) in its own table (save_party_position), then makes party A current: $08 = A, $07 = its size (party_size_of), $57/$58 and $09 from its table (+8, +9, +10), and the view's corner $02 = $57 - $59, $03 = $58 - $5A. $68/$69 is left on party A's table. The game's way of switching party: 27 call sites.
Stores $57, $58 and $09 (column, row, map) at +8, +9 and +10 of the party table at ($68).
A = a party: zeroes its 14-byte table (party_table_ptr). Used for a disband cancelled ($9AB2) and for table 3 after a merge ($99E6).

Ranged fire of the monsters engaged with the current party; battle_round runs it for every party on the battle map through the vector $8E ($9F40). Nothing when every member is dead (party_has_living). For each group 3 to 0 of the party that is in use and hostile (encounter_is_peaceful), and each line 2 to 0 holding a monster: when the line's monster has a ranged weapon class (record byte 5 low nibble, $0413), each of its ten monsters whose flag byte (+$14 + n) is non-zero fires once and the flag is cleared; a monster with no hit points left fires only when its flag has bit 7 set, which damage_monster leaves ($FF, $A70F) on a monster it kills while its flag is still non-zero (the final shot of message 34). A line whose monster is not ranged ends the group at once ($9CAE, JMP $9DDE: the lines after it are skipped). Each shot makes the encounter identified and hostile ($ABD6) and hits when 2d6 (open-ended; under 4 always misses) + record byte 2 + 8 x the fire mode reaches the target number for the group's distance (monster_range_target). Fire mode 2 (weapon classes 11 and 12) fires 3d4 shots ($A992), mode 1 (classes 5 to 7) 1 to 3, mode 0 one. A hit prints 'The <monster>', a verb from the map's message pairs at record +$4B/+$4C (mode 0), +$4D/+$4E (mode 1) or +$4F/+$50 (mode 2) (on map 0: drills or blazes away at, sprays or triggers a burst at, fries or toasts), '...' between shots, and strikes a random member (monster_shot_hits_member). Misses are printed per line ($9DB9). Returns at once if the party is all dead after a shot of mode 1 or 2.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $9CB3: the group monsters_fire is on, 3 down to 0, stored at $9C72; read at $9DDE.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9CB5: the line (2 down to 0) monsters_fire is on, stored at $9C8C; read at $9CE7, $9CFD, $9D45, $9D82, $9DA4, $9DCA and $9DD5.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9CCB: the offset of the flag byte of the monster being tried, $1D (monster 9) down to $14 (monster 0), stored at $9CBC, stepped at $9DAC, read again at $9CD4.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9CE5: the group's distance in feet (group byte 3, stored at $9C84), given to monster_range_target with the line in X.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $9D4B: the shooting monster's fire mode: 0 one shot, 1 (weapon classes 5-7) 1 to 3 shots, 2 (classes 11 and 12) 3d4 shots; stored at $9D1F, just before 8 x the mode is added to its roll ($9D22-$9D28).

Operand of the LDA #imm at $9D7A: the base of the verb message pair for fire mode 1 ($4C: map messages at record +$4D/+$4E) or mode 2 ($4E: +$4F/+$50), stored at $9D62 and $9D55; mode 0 uses $4A ($9D9C).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9DAF: the offset of the high byte of the hit-point word of the monster being tried, $13 (monster 9) down to 1 (monster 0), two a monster, stored at $9CC1.

End of a line in monsters_fire: when shots missed ($9DBA), prints 'n <monsters> miss(es).' (print_byte, print_monster_name with $38 = n, message 31); then the next line, or after line 0 the next group ($9DDE).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9DB9: the shots of the current line that missed, cleared at $9C91 for each line, counted at $9D30.
Next group of monsters_fire, 3 down to 0; after group 0 it returns ($9DB8). Reached also for an empty or peaceful group and, from $9CAE, for a line whose monster is not ranged.
A = low byte, X = high byte of the margin by which the shooting monster's roll beat its target number: the operands $9DE8 and $9DEA, stored at $9D39 and $9D3C.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9DE7: the low byte of the hit margin (num1 - num2, $9D36), stored at $9D39.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $9DE9: the high byte of the hit margin, stored at $9D3C.

A/X = the hit margin, Y = the line: rolls the line's monster damage (monster_damage_roll: record byte 3 d6 + the high nibble of byte 5) into $0235/$0236 and picks a random member 1 to $07. A member with the Evade order (5) escapes when the margin is below 6 (its name, then ' but {0B} nimbly evades.', message 93). Otherwise member_takes_damage ($A85B) applies the damage; when it returns carry set (that member is dead, CON 0) another member is picked, with no limit. Returns carry clear, so the BCS after both calls ($9D88, $9DAA) is never taken.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9E08: the member the shot strikes, random 1 to $07 (stored at $9E02); its order ($89),member is tested for Evade, and it goes to member_takes_damage in Y.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9E10: the high byte of the hit margin (stored at $9DEF); when it is not 0 the member cannot evade.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9E14: the low byte of the hit margin (stored at $9DEC); an evading member escapes when it is below 6.

Carry clear when some member 1 to $07 of the current party has a CON other than exactly 0 (alive, even if down: con_is_zero), carry set when all are dead; the member found (or the last) is left selected. monsters_fire calls it before it starts and after each shot of fire mode 1 or 2.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9E40: the member party_has_living tests, 1 up to $07, stored at $9E35.
Prints 'the ' (game message 67) and the name of line X's monster (print_monster_name) of the encounter record at ($77). Callers: member_attack ($A01A), $A4FD, $AB70.
Entry hidden in the BIT $1AA9 at $9E51 (LDA #$1A): the same with 'The ' (message 26), to start a sentence. Callers: monsters_fire ($9D48), $81F8, $8209, $87C6.

X = a line (0-2) of the encounter record at ($77): prints its monster's name. When the encounter is identified (record byte 9 bit 0, which $ABD6 sets when a monster fires and $ABC9 when a member attacks) the name is string n of the map's monster names (record word +2), n being the monster number, counted from 0; otherwise the kind word, game message 82 + kind: 83 Animal, 84 Mutant, 85 Humanoid, 86 Cyborg, 87 Robot. Singular or plural by $38.
