X = a line (0-2): A = the monster number of that line in the encounter record at ($77) (byte 3, 5 or 7, offset from $BAE9), then falls into monster_record. 14 call sites in the game part.

A = a monster number: points $16/$17 at its eight-byte record in the map's monster table (record word +4, record_address with $45/$46 and $4C = 8) and sets $CA, the pronoun of the text switch {0E}, from pronoun_by_kind ($5B00) indexed by record byte 7. Returns A = $CA, Y = byte 7. Record: +0/+1 hit-point seed, +2 to-hit bonus, +3 damage dice, +4 low nibble armour, +5 weapon class (low nibble) and damage bonus (high), +6 kind (1-5), +7 pronoun index.
X = a line: the damage of that line's monster, record byte 3 d6 + the high nibble of byte 5 (shift_right_4, roll_d6s_plus): X:A = the total. Callers: monster_shot_hits_member ($9DF4) and $8217.
A = byte 5 of the monster record at ($16) AND $0F: the item class of the monster's attack, ranged when 2 to 13 ($0413), as for the members' weapons.

Entry hidden in the BIT $04A0 at $9ED6 (LDY #$04): A = byte 4 of the monster record at ($16) AND $0F, the monster's armour: the dice taken off a member's hit (damage_monster $A664, monster_armour_roll $A738), the multiplier of the kill experience ($A9F9: seed x (armour + 1)) and half of it + 1 the difficulty of the skill roll after an attack ($AA71).
A = byte 7 of the monster record at ($16), the index into pronoun_by_kind ($5B00); called by monster_record and $B965.

Entry hidden in the BIT $06A0 at $9EE0 (LDY #$06): A = byte 6 of the monster record at ($16), the kind 1-5 (Animal, Mutant, Humanoid, Cyborg, Robot: game messages 83-87); also the index of the kind's tile at $5BF5 ($95F5).
A = byte 0, X = byte 1 of the monster record at ($16): the 16-bit hit-point seed (place_encounter_groups rolls a quarter of it plus up to all of it).

A = byte 2 of the monster record at ($16), X = 0: the monster's to-hit bonus, added to its 2d6 roll by monsters_fire ($9D03); plan_group_moves ($84C7) adds 15, 11 or 7 to it in place of a roll, and line_monster_byte2 ($82B1) returns it for melee.

Carry = bit 1 of byte 9 of the encounter record at ($77): set while the encounter is peaceful, clear once it is hostile ($ABD6 clears it when a monster fires, $ABC9 when a member attacks). A = byte 9 / 4.

Last per-party step of a battle round (vector $8E, $B89B): for each conscious member 1 to $07 of the current party, calls the handler of its order ($89),member from order_round_handlers with A = the member ($AC69, JMP ($12)): 1 order_hire, 3 order_weapon, 5 order_evade, 6 order_load_unjam, 7 order_use.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9F0D: the member resolve_orders is on, 1 to $07 (stored at $9F04); its order picks the handler.

RTS of resolve_orders, and the handler order_round_handlers gives orders 0 (none), 2 (Attack: party_ranged_attacks and $7F64 dealt with it), 4 (Run) and 8 (the party's move; both done after the round by resolve_runs_and_moves).

Nine words, the handler of each combat order 0-8, read by resolve_orders: $9F2D (nothing), order_hire $A3F1, $9F2D, order_weapon $A264, $9F2D, order_evade $A37E, order_load_unjam $A383, order_use $A3BC, $9F2D. Orders 0-7 are the indexes of the keys space H A W R E L U in order_keys ($B4BD). Order 8 is the whole party's move, which set_party_move_orders ($B3C7) gives every member. The ninth key, S, never leaves 8: $B449 stores it, then choose_attack_listed ($B4A0) goes back to $B443 with order 2, which replaces it.
High bytes of the words of order_round_handlers, read at $9F18 (LDA $9F2F,Y).

Calls the routine at ($8E) (call_battle_vector) for every party 0 to $0B whose map (+10 of its table) is the battle map $8D, with that party selected (select_party, not restored after); returns A = the number of parties it was called for. battle_round ($B867) runs it with party_ranged_attacks, monsters_fire, $7F64 and resolve_orders, and skips the last three when it returns 0.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9F53: the party for_each_battle_party is on, 0 to $0B (cleared at $9F42, stepped at $9F5E).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9F6A: the number of parties the routine was called for (cleared at $9F45, counted at $9F5B), returned in A.
JMP ($008E): the per-party step for_each_battle_party runs ($9F58).

First per-party step of a battle round (vector $8E, $B87E): every conscious member 1 to $07 of the current party with the Attack order (2) and a reach of 16 or more (member_reach: $FE, a gun with rounds) attacks its target (member_attack).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9F80: the member party_ranged_attacks is on, 1 to $07 (stored at $9F77).

Ranged attack of member A at its target, the target code in its order argument (member_target_code: 12 x party + 3 x group + line). Nothing when that line has nobody alive. Clears the hit list $7E06-$7E35 ($FF ends the three entries at $7E06 and fills the flags at $7E30). $ABC9 makes the target's encounter identified and hostile. The target number for the distance (member_range_target) goes to num2; the member's roll (member_hit_roll: a spoiled roll, jam or failure to detonate, ends the attack), + 8 when the target is in another party's groups, to num1. A miss: '<name> attacks the <monster> and misses.' (messages 28, 32), and the shots are used (1, a burst 3, automatic all), except with class 13, which goes straight to attack_done. A hit with class 13 (explosives): the map's message +$3C, then one damage roll (weapon_damage_roll) strikes every living monster of the group's three lines ($AA90), each kill giving experience ($A9E8). Otherwise by fire mode: single, one hit; burst, 1 to 3 hits while the line lives; automatic, auto_fire_hits hits spread at random over the group's lines while one lives; each through damage_monster ($A618, retried when it picks a dead monster). Then the hit list is reported line by line ($A13D) and the rounds used ($A221, weapon_use_rounds). Ends at attack_done ($9FE0).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9FC9: the attacking member (A at member_attack's entry, stored at $9FA9); read at $9FE0, $9FE6, $A02B, $A051, $A0A7, $A0C1, $A0D3, $A0E3, $A0F0 and $A10F.

Every path of member_attack ends here except the return at $9FB0 (nobody alive on the target line, order and argument left as they are): attack_done ($A53A) with A = the member clears its order and argument and spends a one-shot weapon.
Entry hidden in the BIT $01A9 at $A03A (LDA #$01): a missed single shot uses one round ($A040, weapon_use_rounds).
Entry hidden in the BIT $03A9 at $A03D (LDA #$03): a missed burst uses three rounds. Automatic fire arrives at $A037 and uses every round left (weapon_rounds).

member_attack hit: the weapon class $7E decides. Class 13 (explosives) here: the explosion message (map record +$3C), one damage roll into $71/$72, then for lines 0 to 2 that live and their monsters 0 to 9, $AA90 deals it; a kill (A = 1) gives the member experience ($A9E8: the monster's seed x (armour + 1), add_experience). Then the skill roll ($AA35) and attack_done.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $A08D: the monster (0-9) of the line the explosion is striking, stored at $A069; given to $AA90 in Y ($A079).

member_attack hit with any class but 13, by fire mode (member_fire_mode): burst ($A0B3) 1 to 3 hits on the target line while it has a living monster, 3 rounds; single ($A0DD) one hit, 1 round; automatic ($A0F0) auto_fire_hits hits, each on a random line of the target group while any line lives, every round left. The verb comes from $AB78, $AB86 or $ABA8.

member_attack's report, for each entry of the hit list ($7E06, up to three lines, $FF ends it): with no damage, 'hits n <monsters>' (message 47, count_hit_monsters) and the map's message +$4A (on map 0, ' but fails to inflict any damage'); otherwise a verb pair chosen by the weapon (map record +$3E + 2k and the next: k = 5 for item $11, 4 classes 8-9, 3 classes 10-12, 2 classes 5-7, 1 classes 3-4, else 0) around the line's name, 'n point(s) of damage' ($AA7B), and for kills ' killing him / n of them' or the map's pair at +$5A/+$5B ($ABE1, by the overkill flag $7E30), plus ' just as he peels off a final shot' (message 34) when $7E33 holds a ranged class: the line's weapon class, or 1 when the killed monster's flag byte was already 0 ($A704-$A70A); then '.' (message 90), the skill roll ($AA35) and the next entry. '...' (message 62) joins the results ($E8).

Operand of the LDA #imm at $A15A: in member_attack, first the hits still to land (burst 1 to 3, $A0B8; automatic, auto_fire_hits, $A0F6; counted down at $A0C9 and $A136), then the hit-list entry being reported, 0 to 2 ($A144); read at $A1D2, $A1F3, $A215 and by count_hit_monsters ($A243).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $A1C5: the map record offset of the first message of the verb pair chosen for the weapon ($3E + 2k, stored at $A1BB); the INY reaches the second.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $A1CB: the low byte of the entry's damage total ($7E0C + 2 x entry, stored at $A161), printed by $AA7B.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $A1CD: the high byte of the entry's damage total ($7E0D + 2 x entry, stored at $A168).

Operand of the LDX #imm at $A1E1: how many of the entry's monsters were hit (count_hit_monsters, $A260). With one kill among several hit, A = 0 goes to $ABE1, which the count code prints as 1: 'killing 1 of them'.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $A1FE: the entry's kills ($7E09 + entry, stored at $A1DA), the count $38 of message 34.

member_attack (from $9FA9), continued: the end of its report of one hit-list entry. With a ranged kill kind, $38 = the kills and message 34, 'just as he peels off a final shot'; then '.' (90), attack_skill_improve for the entry's line ($A23A) and flush_line. The next entry (up to 3) goes back to $A144; after the last, $A220 takes the rounds the attack used from the weapon (weapon_use_rounds $BC75) and $A225 jumps to $9FE0 (attack_done).

Operand of LDA #imm at $A220, the end of member_attack's result loop (from $9FA9), written at $A13D: the rounds the attack used, 1 for a single shot ($A0EB), 3 for a burst ($A0CE) or every round left for automatic fire ($A130, $BC73); $A220 hands it to $BC75, which takes it from the weapon's count.

Sets $E8 (a result of this attack has been printed, so the next starts with '...', print_ellipsis_if_more) and prints the name of line attack_line_op of the group at ($77): $9E5D with X = the line, the class word (Animal, Mutant, Humanoid, Cyborg, Robot) or, when bit 0 of the group's byte 9 is set, the monster's own name.
Prints game message 62, '...', when $E8 is set: the second and later results of one attack follow the first on the same line.

Carry clear when line attack_line_op of the attacker's target (attack_target_op, a monster line index 0-47) still has a living monster: line_index_split, then line_alive_count with Y = the line, which leaves $79/$7A on the line's 30-byte record.

Operand of LDA #imm at $A239: the attacking member's target, a monster line index (12 * party + 3 * group + line), written by member_attack at $9FEC (the order parameter AND $3F) and at $A151 (the target of each hit-list entry it reports), and read back by it at $A00A, $A06C, $A09E, $A0BE, $A0E0, $A0FC, $A11C and $A20C.

Operand of LDY #imm at $A23E: the line (0-2) member_attack is working on, written at $A05F and $A119 as it loops over the lines of the target's group and at $A157 (the line of each hit-list entry it reports), read at $A072, $A096, $A122, $A12A and by print_line_name_marked ($A22A).

Counts the monsters of hit-list entry $A15B (the target at $7E06+entry) that took a hit this attack: the non-zero bytes among the ten counters at $7E12 + 10*entry. The count goes to $38 (singular or plural of the message) and to the operand at $A1E2 in member_attack.

Order 3, W)eapon, for member A (already the current character; the order table at $9F2E calls it): prints message 102 ('<name> swaps equipment.'), equips the slot in the member's order parameter ($8B),A through equip_toggle ($0389) and redraws the member's roster line.

After the orders of a battle round (battle_round, $B8A9): for each party 0-$0B (select_party), the first member found with order 8 moves the whole party a square in the direction of its parameter, when anyone is conscious and square_blocked allows: '<names> move.' (print_flagged_names, message 92), the square's action (run_square_action), merge_parties_here, enter_party_map, and the party's orders cleared ($A323). Every conscious member with order 4 (Run) has its direction noted in run_direction_by_record; all orders are cleared, except those of a party whose move failed (nobody conscious, $A326, or square_blocked refusing, $A330), which keeps them. Then each runner, in record order: with four parties already and others in its party, message 88 ('couldn't run.'); otherwise message 43 ('<name> runs.') and, when square_blocked allows, runner_split_off ($98F5) to the new square, run_square_action, merge_parties_here, enter_party_map.

Eight bytes, one per character record 0-7 (0 unused): the direction (0-4 as ask_direction gives it: 0 north, 1 south, 2 west, 3 east, 4 no step) in which that member runs at the end of this round, $FF for none. resolve_runs_and_moves fills it with $FF ($A27A), stores each runner's order parameter ($A2B0) and reads it back ($A2D2, $A2FB).

Order 5, E)vade, for member A: prints message 82 ('<name> evades.') and returns. What evading does is not here: the order stays in the order table ($89) until resolve_runs_and_moves clears it after the round.

Order 6, L)oad/Unjam, for member A: a jammed weapon (bit 7 of its count byte, weapon_count_byte) gets one unjam_weapon try ($0386) and nothing more happens while it stays jammed. A weapon that was not jammed, or has just been freed, is reloaded with a clip of the item its record byte 7 names (weapon_clip_item, find_item, reload_weapon), message 104 ('reloads'); otherwise message 65 ('has no more clips') or, with no clip item, 66 ('weapon can't be reloaded'). Redraws the roster line after a reload.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A38C: the member order_load_unjam is serving, written at its entry ($A383) and read back at $A396 and $A3B6.

Order 7, U)se, for member A: prints message 105 ('<name> uses...'), stops the picture's animation, calls the Use routine $8BEF with A = the high nibble of the member's order parameter, X = its low nibble, Y = the byte at $5BDB + the member's record number and $12 = the member (all chosen when the order was given), then runs the action of the party's square (run_square_action) and restarts the animation. Carry clear.
Operand of LDY #imm at $A3C7: the member order_use is serving, written at $A3BC and read back at $A3D4.
Operand of LDY #imm at $A3E1: the byte at $5BDB + the member's record number, written at $A3D1, passed to the Use routine $8BEF in Y ($B787 stores it when the U)se order is given).

Order 1, H)ire, for member A, the hirer. Nothing when its target line is dead. Needs room (records_in_use $0A below 7, else message 95 'No room in roster.') and a group whose map record ($77) has bit 1 of byte 9 set (peaceful: encounter_is_peaceful $9EF6) and an NPC number in its high nibble (group_npc_number), else the failure message. Copies that NPC's 256-byte record (word n of the map's list 17) to record $0A + 1; unless its byte +$31 is 0 the hirer needs (its CHR + IQ) / 2 + CHR + rank + 2d6 (open) at least the NPC's (CHR + IQ) / 2 + byte +$31 + rank, and a 2d6 under 5 fails at once (the NPC copy's bytes +$2B-+$2D are raised, but that copy is not kept). Success: the NPC joins ($0A and $07 + 1, party table), its message (+$30, map text) is shown, +$31 = the hirer's CHR, +$2B-+$2D drop once per 4 points of margin (acc1 - acc2, which on the no-roll path holds whatever acc1 was), its line's HP words are cleared (it leaves the fight) and each item slot's count gets the item's full load (record byte 4). Failure: messages 44 and 81, '<name> tries to hire the <monster> but fails.'
Operand of LDA #imm at $A44F: the hirer (a party position), written at order_hire's entry ($A3F1) and read at $A4B4, $A4ED and by hire_target_split ($A505).
Operand of LDA #imm at $A490: the hirer's CHR (+$14), taken at $A406 while the hirer is still the current character; stored in the new member's byte +$31 when the hire succeeds ($A494).
Operand of LDY #imm at $A4D3: the record offset of the item slot (+$BD to +$F7, step 2) whose count byte order_hire is filling with the item's full load (item record byte 4), written at $A4C8.

Splits the hirer's target: Y = the hirer (hire_member_op), A = its order parameter AND $3F (member_target_code, a monster line index), then line_index_split ($BDAF) gives A = party, X = group, Y = line.
Adds the current character's byte at record offset Y to the engine's second 16-bit accumulator $71/$72 (char_byte_y, then $07C6, which saturates). Used by order_hire for the NPC's byte +$31 and rank.
A = the current character's CHR (record byte +$14), X = 0: an operand for the engine's accumulator adds ($079D, $07C6).
A = the current character's record byte at offset Y, X = 0 (the high byte for the engine's 16-bit accumulator adds).
A = (CHR + IQ) / 2 of the current character (+$14 plus +$0F, the carry of the sum shifted back in by ROR), X = 0. Both sides of order_hire's test start from it.
Makes record $0A+1, the first character record not in use, the current character (select_character $0338). order_hire copies the NPC there before it knows whether it will join.

For member Y: its target (member_target_code), split (line_index_split $BDAF), counted (line_alive_count $A83C). Carry clear when the target line still has a living monster, A = how many; $79/$7A is left on the line's 30-byte record.
A = member Y's target, a monster line index (12 * party + 3 * group + line, 0-47): its order parameter at ($8B),Y AND $3F (bits 6-7 hold the fire mode, member_fire_mode).

Ends member A's attack (member_attack, $9FE3 and $9FE0): clears its order and order parameter. A weapon whose item record byte 4 is 1 and whose class is 1 or ranged is used up (items 6-12, 14 and 15: Grenade, Plastic explosive, TNT, Mangler, Sabot rocket, LAW rocket, RPG-7, Spear, Throwing knife): its slot is emptied and the weapon field (+$1F) cleared; for class 13 (Grenade, Plastic explosive, TNT) another slot holding the same item becomes the weapon (find_item).
Operand of LDA #imm at $A573: the item number of the weapon attack_done has just used up (written at $A55F), searched for again with find_item to equip the next one of a class-13 item.

Attack roll of member A (select_member): 2d6 with doubles rolling again. A roll under 4 followed by a 1 on a d6 spoils the attack (carry set): classes 8, 9 and 13 'fail to detonate' (message 41), other weapons jam (message 42: count byte $80, rounds lost, roster line redrawn). Otherwise acc1 ($6F/$70) = the roll + DEX (+$13) + 4 * the weapon skill level (weapon_skill_bonus) + 10 for class 13, else +4 in burst mode or + the rounds left in automatic mode; carry clear.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A5BD: the member member_hit_roll is rolling for (written at $A584), used to redraw its roster line after a jam and read at $A5E0 for its fire mode.
A = member Y's fire mode, bits 6-7 of its order parameter ($8B),Y shifted down: 0 single shot, 1 burst, 2 automatic (member_attack's $A02E/$A0AA; $9031 jumps to shift_right_4 inside it).

A = A >> 4: the high nibble of a byte. Shared tail of member_fire_mode; called directly for the use type of an order (order_use), the fire mode in member_hit_roll ($A5E5), a pixel line to a view row ($AEC8) and record nibbles ($9ECE, $B0B1); check_pair_kind jumps to it ($9031).

Runs enter_map ($03B6) for map $8D (the map of the party being dealt with) with $09 set to it for the call, then puts $09 back. resolve_runs_and_moves calls it after moving a party ($A30F, $A367), and encounter after each battle round ($B2A3).
Clears the engine's 24-bit number $1C-$1E (number_0-2), which add_experience ($03DD) adds to the current character's experience.

One hit of member A on monster line Y (0-47): picks one of the line's ten monsters at random (random_monster); carry set when that one is already dead (the caller tries again). Otherwise adds the line to the hit list $7E06 (3 entries, $FF ends it) and counts the hit ($7E12 + 10 * entry + monster), rolls the damage (weapon_damage, with the line's armour dice), sets $D7 for classes 8-9, takes off the armour (monster_armour_absorb) and adds the damage to the line's total ($7E0C, a word per entry, stops at $FFFF). Returns carry clear: A = $FF when the monster lives (or the damage was 0); A = 0 when it died: HP word cleared, $7E09 kill count + 1, its flag byte (+$14 + monster, group_flags_set) set to $FF when it was set, experience (kill_experience) given to the member, overkill flag $D9 (set_overkill), $7E30 &= $D9 and $7E33 = kill_kind_op.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A65C: the monster line index (0-47) damage_monster is hitting, written at $A61B; read at $A639, $A645, $A684, $A6BD and $A713.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A668: the attacking member (party position), written at damage_monster's entry ($A618).
Operand of LDA #imm at $A680: low byte of damage_monster's damage, first the roll (weapon_damage, $A66D), then the damage left after armour ($A68A).
Operand of LDX #imm at $A682: high byte of damage_monster's damage (the roll at $A670, after armour at $A68D).
Operand of LDA #imm at $A6C6: the monster (0-9) within its line that damage_monster picked (random_monster, $A628); also added to the hit counter's index ($A655) and to the status offset ($A6FD).
Operand of LDX #imm at $A6E5: the entry (0-2) of the hit list $7E06 that holds this line, written at $A64B; indexes $7E09, $7E0C, $7E12, $7E30 and $7E33.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A71C: low byte of the killed monster's HP word after the damage was taken off (0 or a negative remainder), written at $A6EC and passed to set_overkill.
Operand of LDX #imm at $A71E: high byte of the remainder (written at $A6F6), for set_overkill.

Operand of LDA #imm at $A72C, stored in $7E33 for the hit-list entry: the line's monster weapon class (record byte 5 bits 0-3, written at $A6BA), or 1 when the killed monster's flag byte was 0 ($A70A). member_attack ($A1F6) adds message 34, 'just as he/she/it/they peel(s) off a final shot', when it is a ranged class.

Rolls the armour of monster line A/X/Y (party, group, line, as line_index_split gives them): line_monster_record, then X = record byte 4 bits 0-3 (the armour dice) and roll_d6s_plus with A = 0. Returns the 16-bit roll in X:A.

Target number of member A's attack (member_attack, $9FD4): the distance from the party to its target group (distance_to_party), the range kind of the member's weapon class (weapon_range_kind on $7E after member_reach) and column 0 when the monster record found is of a ranged class ($0413), 1 (7 more) otherwise, through range_target ($BD48). The record is taken with X = the group number from line_index_split ($A74B), where $9E9F expects a line (0-2).
Operand of LDA #imm at $A75E: the member member_range_target works for (written at $A741), passed to member_reach.
Operand of LDX #imm at $A766: the X that line_index_split returned for the member's target (the group, 0-3), written at $A74B and given to $9E9F, which reads it as a line (0-2).

Target number for monster line X attacking at distance A (tenths of a square, distance_to_party): the line's monster record ($9E9F), its weapon class nibble ($9ED4), weapon_range_kind, then range_target with column 0. Returns A, X = 0. Called at $84B5 (with the distance of a group), $8527 (with the distance of a square one step from the group) and $9CEA.
Calls range_target ($BD48) with the distance A, kind Y and column X set by the caller, and returns X = 0.

Range kind of weapon class A for range_target: Y = 0 for classes 2, 5, 10 and 13 (pistols, thrown weapons, Laser pistol, explosives); 1 for 3, 6, 11 and 8 (Flamethrower, M17 carbine, SMGs, Ion beamer, Laser carbine, Mangler, Sabot rocket); 2 for every other class (1, 4, 7, 9, 12 and up: rifles, assault rifles, LAW, RPG-7, Laser rifle, Meson cannon). A is kept.
Attribute bonus of the current character's LK (+$10). The BITs at $A7BA, $A7BD and $A7C0 hide three more entries: $A7BB DEX (+$13), $A7BE AGL (+$12), $A7C1 ST (+$0E).
Hidden entry (inside BIT $13A0 at $A7BA): LDY #$13, the attribute bonus of DEX.
Hidden entry (inside BIT $12A0 at $A7BD): LDY #$12, the attribute bonus of AGL.
Hidden entry (inside BIT $0EA0 at $A7C0): LDY #$0E, the attribute bonus of ST.
Bonus for the current character's attribute at record offset Y, a signed 16-bit X:A: (value - 12) / 2 for 13 and up, 0 for 9 to 12, and (value - 9) / 2 rounded down (negative, X = $FF) below 9.

Damage of member A's attack: weapon_damage_roll (X = the target's armour dice), plus the member's luck bonus (luck_bonus, signed). A negative sum is not caught: it comes back as a large unsigned X:A (not checked in play).
Operand of ADC #imm at $A7EB: low byte of weapon_damage_roll's result, written at $A7E1.
Operand of ADC #imm at $A7EF: high byte of weapon_damage_roll's result, written at $A7E4.

Dice of member A's weapon (member_reach first; X = the target's armour dice). A melee weapon, or a gun with rounds, rolls its item byte 6 in d6; classes 8 and 9 (Mangler, Sabot rocket, LAW rocket, RPG-7) roll 2 * dice - armour instead when the dice are at least the armour ($FF at most). An empty or jammed gun (reach 15) is swung: 1d6 for classes 2 and 10, 2d6 otherwise, and the class number is added (A = $7E at the JMP; the LDA #$00 at $A809 is overwritten). Result in X:A (roll_d6s_plus).
Operand of CPX #imm at $A823: the target's armour dice (X at weapon_damage_roll's entry, written at $A7F4), also subtracted at $A82C.
Operand of ADC #imm at $A830: the weapon's damage dice (item record byte 6), written at $A827, so classes 8-9 roll 2 * dice - armour.

Counts the living monsters (HP word non-zero) of monster line A/X/Y (party, group, line; group_line_ptr leaves $79/$7A on it). Carry clear with A = the count when there is one, carry set with A = 0 when none.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A853: line_alive_count's count of monsters with a non-zero HP word, cleared at $A841 and incremented at $A84D.

Party member Y takes X:A points of damage, with the messages ($C8 non-zero: not from a monster; $A0 non-zero: armour ignored). Carry set, nothing done, when the member is dead (CON 0). A member already down (CON negative) is always hit by $C8 damage; otherwise a monster whose weapon class (record byte 5 bits 0-3) is ranged misses ('but misses.'), a melee one hits when 2d6 (open) is below its record byte 3; that test is never reached, since a monster's melee picks only conscious members ($81B7-$81C7) and member_takes_damage has three callers, $821D, $90BC and $9E23. Armour: AC (+$1A) in d6 off the damage. Then CON is reduced (con_subtract): reaching 0 makes it -1, below -49 makes it 0 (dead); a member going down keeps its CON from before the hit in +$26/+$27 and gets ' and ' + its condition (wound_messages). Ends with '.' and the roster line; carry clear.

Operand of LDA #imm at $A892: the attacker's weapon class, the low nibble of byte 5 of the monster record at $16 ($9ED4, written at $A86E); 1 (melee), with nothing left after the armour and the member's AC 0 (member_ac_op), gives ' but misses.' ($A8EE).
Operand of LDA #imm at $A8F5: the member's AC (+$1A), written at $A8BF; 0 with a melee attacker turns a fully absorbed hit into ' but misses.'.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A963: the member taking the damage (Y at member_takes_damage's entry, written at $A861), whose roster line is redrawn at the end.
Sets both bytes of the current character's CON (+$1D/+$1E) to A: $FF makes it -1, 0 makes it 0 (dead).
Copies the current character's record word at offset Y to $027A/$027B (member_takes_damage: the CON at +$1D, or +$26 for a member already down).

Game message numbers for condition_index 0-5: 49 'knocks him/her unconscious', 50 'seriously wounds', 51 'critically wounds', 52 'mortally wounds', 53 'knocks comatose', 25 'rips him/her to shreds' (dead).
Number of hits of member A's automatic fire (member_attack, $A0F3): select_member, the rounds left in its weapon (weapon_rounds), then auto_fire_dice.
Rolls max(1, A / 4) d4 and returns the total in A (also entered here by $9D5A with A set by the caller).
Operand of ADC #imm at $A9A4: the running total of auto_fire_dice's d4 rolls, cleared at $A994.

Damage X:A against monster line Y (0-47): rolls the line's armour (monster_armour_roll) and, unless $D7 is set (classes 8 and 9, damage_monster), takes it off the damage, stopping at 0. Clears $D7 and returns the damage in X:A.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A9C4: low byte of the damage (A at monster_armour_absorb's entry), replaced by what is left after the armour ($A9C9).
Operand of SBC #imm at $A9C7: low byte of the monster's armour roll (monster_armour_roll, written at $A9BA).
Operand of LDA #imm at $A9CC: high byte of the damage (X at the entry), replaced by what is left ($A9D0).
Operand of SBC #imm at $A9CE: high byte of the armour roll (written at $A9BD).

Experience for killing a monster of line A (0-47): the 16-bit base in the line's monster record (bytes 0/1, monster_exp_base) times (its armour dice + 1), left in the 24-bit number $1C-$1E for add_experience ($03DD).
Operand of LDX #imm at $A9F4: the line (0-2) from line_index_split, written at $A9EB, for the monster record ($9E9F).
Operand of ADC #imm at $AA13: low byte of the monster's experience base, added armour dice + 1 times.
Operand of ADC #imm at $AA19: high byte of the monster's experience base.
$1C/$1D = word 0 of the monster record at ($16), $1E = 0: the experience base (the same word seeds the monsters' hit points in place_encounter_groups, $936E).

After member's attack on monster line A: the current character may learn from it (skill_improve_roll $020F) in the skill of its equipped weapon (item_skill_number; Fists, item 0, with none), at difficulty (the line's armour dice / 2) + 1. Nothing when the weapon is of a ranged class and empty (weapon_rounds 0).

Operand of LDA #imm at $AA58: the equipped weapon's item number (written at $AA3F), whose skill attack_skill_improve tests. $AA58 is reached by the branches at $AA4B and $AA52; from $AA55 it is skipped by the BIT at $AA57 and A = 0 (Fists).
Operand of LDA #imm at $AA5E: the monster line index (0-47) attack_skill_improve was given (written at $AA35).
Operand of LDX #imm at $AA6C: the line (0-2) from line_index_split (written at $AA63), for the monster record.
Prints the number X:A (print_word) and message 89, ' point(s) of damage', singular when X:A is 1 ($38 = 1, else 2).

Monster Y (0-9) of monster line A takes the damage in $71/$72 (melee at $814C, explosives at $A07C). Carry set when it is already dead. Armour is taken off (monster_armour_absorb); none left prints the name and the map's message at record +$4A ('but fails to inflict any damage'). Otherwise its HP word is reduced (0 at most), and the line reads: class 13 '...' between victims, ' at '; other classes one of the map's messages at +$52/+$53 ('beats', 'hammers'); the monster's name; class 13 one of +$58/+$59; ' for ', the points of damage; a kill: set_overkill and print_killing. Ends '.', returns carry clear with A = 1 for a kill, 0 otherwise.
Operand of LDY #imm at $AACC: the monster line index (A at monster_takes_damage's entry); read by takes_line_ptr ($AB56) and given to monster_armour_absorb.
Operand of ORA #imm at $AAD7: high byte of the damage left after armour (written at $AAD4); also read by the SBC at $AAFB and at $AB33.
Operand of LDY #imm at $AAEF: 2 * the monster number (Y at the entry), the offset of its HP word in the line record.
Operand of SBC #imm at $AAF4: low byte of the damage left after armour (written at $AAD1); read again at $AB30.
Operand of LDA #imm at $AB3E: low byte of the killed monster's HP word after the damage (0 or negative, written at $AB0C), for set_overkill.
Operand of LDX #imm at $AB40: high byte of that remainder (written at $AB16).
Operand of LDA #imm at $AB52: 1 when monster_takes_damage killed the monster (incremented at $AB07), 0 otherwise; the value it returns in A.
monster_takes_damage's line: line_index_split of takes_line_op, the line (0-2) kept in $AB6F, then group_line_ptr ($79/$7A = the line record).
A = low OR high byte of the HP word of the monster at takes_hp_offset_op in the line at ($79): zero when it is dead or absent.
Prints the monster's name in the singular (set_count_one, then $9E4F with X = the line, takes_line_x_op), then puts $38 back.
Operand of LDX #imm at $AB6E: the line (0-2) of monster_takes_damage's target, written at $AB5C.
Operand of LDA #imm at $AB73: the text count $38 as it was at monster_takes_damage's entry (written at $AA9A), put back after printing the name.
Burst fire phrase (member_attack, $A0BB): the map's message at record +$39 ('discharges a burst') for classes 5-7, +$3A ('Sub-atomic particles burst from') for the others, then ' and '.

Single shot phrase (member_attack, $A0DD), by the weapon class $7E: the map's message at record +$37 for class 2, +$38 for 3-7, +$3D for 8-9, +$3A for the rest; then ' and '. Map 8's wording: 'attacks', 'triggers', 'lauches a shell' (sic), 'Sub-atomic particles burst from'.
Automatic fire phrase (member_attack, $A0F9): the map's message at record +$3B ('fires full auto') for classes 5-7, +$3A for the others, then ' and '.
Shows the map message whose number is at record offset Y (show_map_msg_at), then ' and '.
Prints game message 45, ' and '.
Prints game message 97, ' at '.
A = the high nibble of byte 9 of the group's map record at ($77): the number of the NPC (map list 17) who can be hired from it.

For member A's target: its group's map record (member_target_code, line_index_split, group_ptr, group_square_record) gets bit 0 of byte 9 set (the monsters' own names are shown, $9E4F) and bit 1 cleared (no longer peaceful, so it cannot be hired). Called when a member attacks ($80FB, $9FCC).
Byte 9 of the group's map record at ($77): bit 0 set, bit 1 cleared (also entered here by $9CDF).
Kill message for A monsters ($38 = A): game message 98 ' killing him/her/it/n of them', or with the overkill flag $D9 set one of the map's messages at record +$5A/+$5B (show_map_msg_pair $59).
Overkill flag from a killed monster's HP word X:A after the damage (0 or negative): $D9 = 0 when it is 0 to -14, 1 below (the two bytes are tested separately, so -256 also gives 0).
Hidden entry inside the BIT $01A9 at $ABFE: LDA #$01, the branch target of set_overkill's two tests; then $D9 = A.
Carry clear for weapon classes 10-12 (class_10_to_12) and 5-7 (class_5_to_7), the classes that offer B)urst and A)uto fire ($B513, $B5C7); carry set otherwise.
Carry clear when A is weapon class 5, 6 or 7 (in the item table: the Mac 17 and Uzi SMGs are class 6, the AK 97 and M1989A1 assault rifles class 7; no item is class 5), set otherwise.
CLC, RTS: the 'yes' exit shared by class_5_to_7, class_10_to_12 and class_8_or_9.
Carry clear when A is weapon class 10, 11 or 12 (Laser pistol; Ion beamer, Laser carbine; Laser rifle, Meson cannon), set otherwise.
Carry clear when A is weapon class 8 or 9 (Mangler, Sabot rocket; LAW rocket, RPG-7), set otherwise.
A = the count byte of the current character's equipped weapon slot (weapon_slot_offset + 1): bit 7 set when jammed, bits 0-5 the rounds; Y = its offset.
A = byte 7 of the equipped weapon's item record (weapon_record): the item number of its clip, 0 for none.
A = 10 * Y (Y = 0 gives 0).

Monster record of party A, group X, line Y: $79/$7A = the group (group_ptr), $77/$78 = its map record (group_square_record), then $9E9F with X = the line: $16/$17 = the record of the line's monster type, $CA its pronoun.
Operand of LDX #imm at $AC57: the line (Y at line_monster_record's entry, written at $AC4E).
A = a random monster number 0-9 (random_1_to_a 10, minus 1), Y = 2 * A, the offset of its HP word.
JMP ($0012): calls the routine whose address was put in work_ptr (square class handlers, step routines, order handlers, and the map's own routines that run_action calls at $886F).
Keys 1-7 of the main loop ($7EB4): the character screen of party member A (view_character), then redraw_view and after_move.

After the party moves or the view is redrawn: party_square, redraw_special_squares, draw_markers, merge_parties_here ($9959); if anyone is conscious, run_square_action, restore_view_if_covered and encounter_if_engaged.
JMP encounter_if_engaged: after_move's last step, also called by the main loop ($7E9E) and $9BAB.
Clears the message area ($0320), then draw_view.

Draws the map view afresh, keeping $5F/$60: party_square, draw_whole_view (19 x 9 squares and the frame), redraw_special_squares, $94CF for map $09 (scan_for_encounters drawing the monsters' tiles; $8D kept), draw_markers.

Draws what sits on the view: the other parties on this map (draw_other_parties), the party's own marker (draw_party_marker), the clock and the Geiger counter check (print_clock), the Geiger gauge (draw_geiger_gauge).

Runs the action of the square the party stands on (view_center): square_class_action, again for as long as the handler returns carry set (most end with alter_party_square, carry set when the square was changed); a class 2 square only when its flags let the party walk on (checks_square_passable $8F72, bit 7 of square_flags). Then $02AA = 0 and square_at_view_center ($C6/$C7).
Calls the handler of the party square's class from square_class_handlers, with $5F/$60 on its action record ($B12D) and X/Y = the square (view_center).

Handler of each square class 0-15 (square_class_action): 0 $AE0D (nothing), 1 $BDE9 (square_messages), 2 $8E14, 3 $AE0D, 4 $833D, 5 $9194, 6 $8839 (action byte), 7 $AE0D, 8 $88E3, 9 $82E0, 10 $89A3, 11 $AE0D, 12 $8878, 13-15 $AE0D.
Second byte of each square_class_handlers word: square_class_action reads the high bytes through $ACF4,Y (Y = 2 * class).

Marks the other parties on the view: for each party $0B down to 0 but the current one ($08), on this map ($09, party table +$0A) and in view (square_in_view, table +$08/+$09), tile 9 at its square (square_to_screen, draw_tile; while the roster is shown, not at pixel line 14 and down, so only on the view's top row). Puts $68/$69 back on the current party.
Operand of LDA #imm at $AD4F: the party draw_other_parties is looking at, from $0B ($AD15) down to 0.

Can the party step in direction A? The square one step from the party's (step_from_view_corner on $02/$03) is refused (carry set) when off the map, of class 15 (monster groups) or 3, or by $8DEC (class 2 squares), $8A36 (a class 10 square may ask 'Enter new location (Y/N)?') or bump_blocking_square ($915E). Returns X/Y = that square (move_target); for a step off the map, which is not stored, the square tested before.
X/Y = the square square_blocked last tested (its operands $AD8F and $AD91).
Operand of LDX #imm at $AD8E: column of the square square_blocked is testing (written at $AD64).
Operand of LDY #imm at $AD90: row of the square square_blocked is testing (written at $AD67).
X/Y = the party's square one step in direction A: step_from_view_corner on the view's top-left square $02/$03 (callers $8BD8, $8DD9).
X/Y + the view offsets $59/$5A (add_view_offset: the party's square for the view corner X/Y), then step_square in direction A.

Moves square X/Y one step in direction A (0 north, 1 south, 2 west, 3 east, 4 none, 5 north-west, 6 north-east, 7 south-west, 8 south-east) through step_routines; carry set when the result is off the map (square_on_map).
Operand of LDY #imm at $ADAB: Y at step_square's entry (written at $AD9C), put back before the step routine runs.
Step routine: X + 1, Y - 1 (north-east).
Step routine: Y - 1 (north).
Step routine: X - 1, Y + 1 (south-west).
Step routine: Y + 1 (south).
Step routine: Y - 1, X - 1 (north-west).
Step routine: X - 1 (west).
Step routine: Y + 1, X + 1 (south-east).
Step routine: X + 1 (east).

step_square's routine for each direction 0-8: $ADB4 north, $ADB7 south, $ADBA west, $ADBD east, $04D5 none (square_on_map only), $ADB9 north-west, $ADB3 north-east, $ADB6 south-west, $ADBC south-east.
Second byte of each step_routines word: step_square reads the high bytes through $ADC0,Y (Y = 2 * direction).
Moves the party one square in direction A (0-4) if it can: restore_view_if_covered, square_blocked; carry set when refused, else move_party.

Moves the party in direction A without the checks (also called by use_succeeded at $8CB5): carry set when nobody is conscious. Otherwise, outside combat the party's square is redrawn without its marker (redraw_party_square), the view is moved by view_scrolls[A] (called through move_scroll_op), then party_square and advance_clock; carry clear.
Operand of LDA #imm at $ADEA: the direction move_party was given (written at $ADDF), the index into view_scrolls.
Operand of the JSR at $AE04: the view routine for the direction (view_scrolls, written at $ADF1/$ADF7); $FFFF as loaded; $AE0D (nothing) in the listing's snapshot is the last value written.
High byte of the JSR operand at $AE04 (written at $ADF7 from view_scrolls_hi); the low byte is move_scroll_op.
CLC, RTS: square class handler for classes 0, 3, 7, 11 and 13-15, and the view routine for direction 4.
View routine for each direction 0-4 (move_party): $AE2F north, $AE8C south, $AE4E west, $AE6D east, $AE0D none.
Second byte of each view_scrolls word: move_party reads the high bytes through $AE10,Y (Y = 2 * direction) into move_scroll_hi_op.
Hot key I of the main menu (handler table word at $7F26): try_move_party north (0); when it moves, step_done.

Hot key left arrow ($1B in the bar's hot-key list; key table entry 6, $9B) of the main menu ($7F2E), and the main loop's start when $92 is set ($7E60): try_move_party with direction 4, no step, so the clock advances (advance_clock) and the square's action runs again (step_done, after_move).
After a step: the step sound (play_sound_16), random_encounter, then after_move.
View one square north: $03 - 1; outside combat the picture is scrolled down (scroll_map_down) and view rows 1 and 0 redrawn (draw_view_row with $37 = $10, then 0).
Hot key J of the main menu (handler table word at $7F2A): try_move_party west (2); when it moves, step_done.
View one square west: $02 - 1; outside combat the picture is scrolled right (scroll_map_right) and view columns 1 and 0 redrawn (draw_view_column with $36 = 2, then 0).
Hot key L of the main menu (handler table word at $7F2C): try_move_party east (3); when it moves, step_done.
RTS: the exit of view_north, view_west, view_east and view_south in combat ($D8 set), and of cmd_east when refused.
View one square east: $02 + 1; outside combat the picture is scrolled left (scroll_map_left) and view columns 17 and 18 redrawn (draw_view_column with $36 = $22, then $24).
Hot key K of the main menu (handler table word at $7F28): try_move_party south (1); when it moves, step_done.
View one square south: $03 + 1; outside combat the picture is scrolled up (scroll_map_up) and view rows 7 and 8 redrawn (draw_view_row with $37 = $70, then $80).
Draws view column $36 / 2: the nine squares from row $03 down at map column $02 + $36 / 2 (draw_square, $0216 counting).
Operand of LDX #imm at $AEB6: the map column draw_view_column draws (written at $AEA9).
Operand of LDY #imm at $AEB8: the map row of the next square, from $03 ($AEAE), incremented at $AEBD.
Draws view row $37 / 16: the $54 (view_columns) squares from column $02 at map row $03 + $37 / 16 (draw_square, $021D counting).
Operand of LDX #imm at $AEDB: the map column of the next square, from $02 ($AED3), incremented at $AEE2.
Operand of LDY #imm at $AEDD: the map row draw_view_row draws (written at $AECE).

Draws the whole view: $6A (roster), $B7 (text window) and $B8 = 0, the nine rows (draw_view_row with $37 = 0, $10 ... $80), then the frame from column 0, row 0 to column 37, row 17 (draw_frame). Keeps the cursor and window (push_zp23).
Operand of LDA #imm at $AF00: the $37 of the row draw_whole_view has just drawn (written at $AEF8), stepped by $10 to $90.
Draws the party's marker, tile 7, on its square (party_square, square_to_screen, draw_tile).
Inverse off, then draws the party's square $57/$58 as the map has it (draw_square), taking the marker off.

Time for one step on this map: the clock $0C/$0D/$0E advances by the record's bytes +$34 (fraction) and +$35 (minutes), 60 minutes an hour, 24 hours; $D2 and the 24-bit count $04-$06 (overflow into $F4FD) by byte +$36. Every time the low nibble of $D2 comes to 0, health_tick ($B795).

Sets $9F (distance to the nearest class 9 square) to $FF, then draws again every square of the view (9 rows from $03, $54 columns from $02) that is on the map and of class 4, 5 or 9 (draw_square, which also sets $9F for class 9).
X/Y = the square redraw_special_squares is looking at (its operands $AFD2 and $AFD4).
Operand of LDX #imm at $AFD1: the map column redraw_special_squares is at (written at $AF9B).
Operand of LDY #imm at $AFD3: the map row redraw_special_squares is at (written at $AF89).
RTS of scan_square, also advance_clock's exit when no health tick is due ($AF79).
Carry set when a party, any of 0 to $0B including the current one, stands on map $09 at square X/Y (party table +$08/+$09/+$0A); carry clear when none. X/Y are kept; $68/$69 end on the current party.
Operand of LDA #imm at $B003: the party party_at_square has just tested, from $0B (written at $AFDE) down.
$68/$69 back on the current party's table (party_table_ptr $08), carry clear, X/Y = party_at_square's square.
Operand of LDX #imm at $B010: the column party_at_square was given (written at $AFD6).
Operand of LDY #imm at $B012: the row party_at_square was given (written at $AFD9).

Random encounter after a step: 1 chance in N, N = map record byte +$2F (0: never). Needs a free entry among the first +$32 of the map's list 15 (groups; bytes 3, 5 and 7 zero; $65 = its number). The monster type is 1 to byte +$31 at random; by its weapon class (monster record byte 5 bits 0-3) the entry's bytes 0 and 1 come from group_party_range and group_monster_range, and the distance in squares from $5B93 (1, 3 or 4). From the party's square, a random direction (not 4) is walked that many squares, each on the map, not at column or row 0, of class 0 and without a party (party_at_square); failing that the next direction, then a square nearer. The entry gets line 0 = the type with 1 to (monster record byte 4 / 16) monsters, and the square class 15 with byte $65 (set_square).
Operand of LDA #imm at $B086: the direction random_encounter is walking (written at $B075).
Operand of LDA #imm at $B0BD: the monster type random_encounter chose (written at $B04C), stored as line 0's type (list 15 entry byte 3).
Operand of CMP #imm at $B0D1: the first direction random_encounter tried (written at $B071); coming back to it, it tries one square nearer.
X/Y = the last square random_encounter reached (its operands $B0E7 and $B0E9).
Operand of LDX #imm at $B0E6: the column random_encounter reached (written at $B092).
Operand of LDY #imm at $B0E8: the row random_encounter reached (written at $B095).

Byte 0 of a random encounter's group record, by the monster's weapon class 0-12, in distance_to_party's unit (tenths of a square): 15, 35, 40, 65, 90, 40, 65, 90, 65, 90, 40, 65, 90. Within it scan_for_encounters ($95C9) draws the group's monster tile on the view, and starts the fight when the party's reach ($F4E1) covers the distance too ($9620). A class above 12 would read on into group_monster_range.

Byte 1 of a random encounter's group record, by weapon class 0-12, in tenths of a square (distance_to_party): 15, 15, 40, 65, 90, 40, 65, 90, 65, 90, 40, 65, 90; within it scan_for_encounters starts the fight whatever the party's reach ($9618). A class above 12 would read the code at $B105.

Changes the party's square ($57/$58) as its action record says at offset A (alter_square $042E: the class and byte there; class $FE trades places with the square saved by the last change, $FD does that and stops, any other byte with bit 7 set writes nothing). Carry set when the square was written, so run_square_action runs the new square's handler; carry clear ends that loop. The last step of most square handlers (8 callers, e.g. $8840 with A = 1 after a class 6 action).
Outside combat, when the text window ($B7) or the roster ($6A) covers the view, redraws it (redraw_view); otherwise nothing.
Carry clear when square X/Y is inside the view: 0 <= X - $02 < $54 and 0 <= Y - $03 < 9 (unsigned); carry set otherwise.
SEC, RTS: square_in_view's 'no' exit.
For square X/Y: A = its class, and $5F/$60 on its action record, entry (its byte) of the class's list (map_square_at, action_record).
$C6 = the class and $C7 = the byte of the party's square (view_center, map_square_at).

Prints the clock, hours ($0E) ':' minutes ($0D), two digits each at column $21 of row 0 (direct output, window kept), then looks for item $30, the Geiger counter, in members 1 to $07 (find_item): when nobody carries one, $9F = $FF (the gauge shows nothing).
Operand of LDA #imm at $B185: the member print_clock is searching for a Geiger counter (item $30), from 1 ($B176).
Looks for encounters on map $09 ($8D = $09, $94CF with drawing); when one is found (carry clear) the fight starts (encounter). A = 1 and carry set otherwise.

The fight, the main menu's Enc ($7F1A) and encounter_if_engaged: $D8 = 1, each record's experience saved ($F486: records in use, then 3 bytes each). Rounds (encounter_round): each party in turn whose map has a fight (group_map_slots $5B8F) or is the map in memory ($91), or whose player agrees (messages 54 and 76), gets its map loaded, encounters placed (scan_for_encounters, place_encounter_groups, groups_measure), then every party on that map gives its orders (get_party_orders); 'Use these options' (Y) runs battle_round ($B867) and writes the groups back. The fight ends when no map is left in group_map_slots (encounter_end), or at once when no party has given an order and no round has run ($B288).

Operand of LDA #imm at $B1CD: first the record (1-7) whose experience encounter saves ($B1B2), then the party being dealt with ($B1F2), then in encounter_end the record whose experience gain is reported ($B32E, $B369).
Start of a round: clears the four parties' done flags $F4DD-$F4E0, then $B1F2 with party 0.

Deals with party Y in this round (skipped when its done flag $F4DD+Y is set): select_party; its map $8D fights when it is in group_map_slots or is the map in memory ($91), or, with someone conscious, when the player says Y to messages 54 and 76; then the map is loaded, the encounters placed and every party on it gives its orders; the round runs when anyone has orders (or a round has run) and the options are accepted.

Operand of LDA #imm at $B251: the party whose orders $B1F2 is taking ($B249-$B282), then the party encounter_party_done marks ($B2F8), then in encounter_end the offset of each record's saved experience at $F486 ($B32A, $B337, $B353).
Operand of LDA #imm at $B284: how many parties on this map have given an order this round (incremented at $B275).
Operand of ORA #imm at $B286: 1 once a battle round has run in this fight ($B297), 0 from encounter's start; with no orders and no round run, the fight ends.
Marks every party on map $8D done for this round ($F4DD+party = 1); the fight goes on (encounter_next_party) while group_map_slots holds a map, else encounter_end.

End of the fight: the party chosen at the start ($B6) again, each record whose experience grew gets '<name> gains n experience.' (messages 39 and 40), $D8 = 0, its map reloaded (enter_map) and the view redrawn.
Next party ($B1F2 with $B1CE + 1); after the last one: the round's time (advance_clock, health_tick), six lines scrolled out, and the next round (encounter_round).

Orders of the current party: clears its members' orders; with someone conscious, asks each member (orders_member_loop $B40A) when any of its four groups is in use (group byte 0 non-zero), else messages 20 and 76 ('This party is not being attacked. Do you want them to execute a battle round (Y/N)?', $B3F0 on). Carry clear when nobody is conscious, when the answer is N (or left-arrow) and when the orders are given; carry set when left-arrow backs out past the first conscious member ($B487), and encounter then takes every party's orders again ($B265).
Gives every member of the party order 8 (move the party) with parameter A AND $7F, the direction ($B469); carry clear.

Operand of LDA #imm at $B3CE: the member (1 to the party's count $07) orders_member_loop is asking, set at $B40F/$B412, lowered at $B482 and read at $B415, $B420, $B443, $B457, $B46C, $B471 and $B47A; then the direction set_party_move_orders puts in each member's order parameter (written at $B3C9).
Operand of LDX #imm at $B3EB: the group get_party_orders is looking at, from 3 down to 0 ($B3DD).

Waits for the answer to get_party_orders' question for a party that no encounter group is attacking ('This party is not being attacked. Do you want them to execute a battle round (Y/N)?', messages 20 and 76, printed at $B3F6-$B3FD): ask_yes_no with the portrait animation turned back on. Y goes on to orders_member_loop; N or left-arrow returns at $B478 with carry clear and the party's orders still 0, as $B3B9 cleared them.

Asks each conscious member of party $08 for a combat order (after $B3E9 when one of the party's four encounter groups exists, or Y at $B400): shows the encounter's picture (encounter_portrait), then for members 1 to $07 highlights the roster line, prints the name and message 55 ', choose: R)un U)se H)ire E)vade A)ttack W)eapon L)oad/Unjam' and waits for one of order_keys. The order (the key's index; S, index 8, is rewritten as 2 by choose_attack_listed) goes to ($89)+member and the handler's result A to ($8B)+member (order_handlers, JMP ($12) at $AC69). A handler returning carry set asks the same member again; left-arrow goes back to the previous conscious member and, past the first, returns carry set. A party Run (order 4, A bit 7) gives every member order 8 and the direction ($B3C7). Ends with carry clear.

Operand of the LDX # at $B45F: the order just chosen, written at $B446: 0-7 when it is read, since S's 8 is replaced by 2 when choose_attack_listed goes back to $B443. Compared with 4 (Run) at $B461: a Run result with bit 7 set (P)arty) becomes the party move at $B3C7.

Order key space (order 0): keeps the portrait animation flag $AC, turns the animation off, draws the map view ($AC8C), waits for a key, then shows the roster ($02B7) and the picture window ($0416) again and restores $AC. Returns carry set, so the member is asked again.

Order key S (index 8 of order_keys; the prompt does not name it): drops the return address of the JSR $AC69 at $B45A and goes back to $B443 as A)ttack (order 2) with $025A = 0, so for a player character choose_attack shows the group list even when only one line is in reach; an NPC (record +$29 non-zero) still chooses its line itself ($B50B), as with A.

Order handler table, one word per key of order_keys (the key's index is the order, except S: index 8 runs choose_attack_listed, which makes it 2): 0 space choose_view_map, 1 H choose_hire, 2 A choose_attack, 3 W choose_weapon, 4 R choose_run, 5 E $B478 (CLC/RTS: Evade takes no argument), 6 L choose_load, 7 U choose_use, 8 S choose_attack_listed. Read at $B44D/$B452 into $12/$13 and run through JMP ($12) at $AC69 with A = the member.
High bytes of order_handlers' words, read by LDA $B4AC,Y at $B452 (the low bytes by LDA $B4AB,Y at $B44D).

Keys of the combat order prompt, for wait_listed_key at $B43E: space H A W R E L U S ($A0 $C8 $C1 $D7 $D2 $C5 $CC $D5 $D3), zero-terminated; the index is the order number 0-7, except S, index 8, which choose_attack_listed turns into order 2 (A)ttack); order 8 is the party move ($B3C7).

Order A (Attack) for member A (1-7, kept at $B4DA): a weapon whose count byte has bit 7 is refused with message 56 'Your weapon is jammed.'; with no monster line in the member's reach, message 80 'Reload your weapon.' for a ranged weapon with no rounds, otherwise 57 'No one is within range.'; refusals return carry set. Then $B500. Returns carry clear with A = fire mode * 64 + line index (0-47; modes 0 single, 1 burst, 2 automatic), carry set when cancelled.
Operand of the LDA # at $B4D9: the member choose_attack works for (1-7), written on entry ($B4C7) and read as data at $B5B8 for member_reach.
BIT $39A9 skips the LDA #$39 at $B4F1 when coming from $B4EE

Thresholds for an NPC's fire mode (choose_attack, $B551), indexed by how many characters (records 1 to $0A) are not conscious: a d10 at or above the entry fires automatic, below it burst. $FF 9 7 5 3 0 0 0: never, 20, 40, 60, 80 %, then always. Used only for automatic weapons with more than 3 rounds.
Lines in reach (A = their number, kept in $4E). An NPC (record +$29 non-zero) chooses line and fire mode itself from $B50B; a player character goes to $B59B.

NPC: a melee reach (under 16 feet) takes the first line in reach as a single attack ($B58A). A weapon not of an automatic class ($AC04) fires single; an automatic one fires single with fewer than 3 rounds, burst with exactly 3, and with more, burst or automatic by auto_fire_thresholds and a d10.
Operand of the LDA # at $B53D: the record (1 to $0A) whose consciousness is being tested, written at $B52F.
Operand of the LDY # at $B54D: how many of records 1 to $0A are not conscious (zeroed at $B52A, counted at $B53A); it indexes auto_fire_thresholds at $B551.

Picks one of the $4E lines in reach at random: $0252 counts down a d($4E) while list items are tried in turn with group_list_line, output off ($A1 = 1). Returns carry clear with A = mode * 64 + line index.
Operand of the LDY # at $B573: the list item (line index + 1) tried by the random pick, written at $B566; the DEC at $B57D turns the chosen item into its line index.
Operand of the LDA # at $B580: the fire mode of an automatic choice, written at $B557 (0 single, 1 burst, 2 automatic) or $B58C (0, for a melee reach and for a player's only line).
Mode 0 (single) and the first line in reach ($0252 = 1): for an NPC's melee reach, and for a player's only line.
Player, only one line in reach, key A: the line is taken without the list (Y = its index), and the fire mode is settled from $B5B8 as for a listed choice.

Player character: with one line in reach and key A ($025A = 1) the line is taken at once ($B593); otherwise group_list_show and list_choose, where left-arrow ($FF) returns carry set, $FD/$FE wait again, and the chosen line flashes.

Y = the chosen line index. A melee reach, a weapon not of an automatic class, or fewer than 3 rounds give a single attack ($B611, $B60A); otherwise 'S)ingle B)urst' (message 58), 'A)uto' (59) with 4 rounds or more, '?' (60), and one of fire_mode_keys up to the allowed mode; left-arrow returns carry set.

Operand of the LDA # at $B5E6: the highest fire mode the weapon allows, written at $B5DE: 1 (burst) with exactly 3 rounds, 2 (automatic) with 4 or more. It decides whether 'A)uto' (message 59) is offered ($B5E8) and bounds the key at $B603.
Operand of the ORA # at $B60D: the chosen line index (0-47), written at $B5BB and read as data at $B611 for a single attack.
Single attack: A = the line index (mode 0), carry clear.
Keys of the fire mode question (choose_attack, $B5FE): S B A ($D3 $C2 $C1), zero-terminated; the index is the mode, 0 single, 1 burst, 2 automatic.

Shows the list of monster lines for Attack and Hire, A = how many are in reach: $4E = A + 1, title message 63 'Which group?', item numbers wrap at 65 ($4D = $41: items 1-64, of which only line indexes 0-47 exist), nothing marked ($D1 = $FF), from item 1 ($4A), each line printed by group_list_line ($47/$48 = $B63D); ends in list_show_page ($03A4).

Per-item routine of the group list, item A (1-64): line index A-1, split by line_index_split into party, group and line. Carry set (item left out) unless the group passes group_in_reach and the line's count byte (+4/+6/+8) is non-zero; otherwise prints the list label (inverse when the group belongs to the current party $08), the count and the monster's name (print_line_count_name), then the distance in feet right-aligned at the window's edge and an apostrophe; carry clear.
Operand of the LDY # at $B654: the item's line (0-2) from line_index_split, written at $B646; it picks the count offset in line_count_offsets and is read at $B670 for print_line_count_name.
Operand of the CMP # at $B663: the party (0-3) whose group record the item belongs to, written at $B643; when it is the current party $08 the item's label is printed in inverse.
Operand of the LDA # at $B684: the group's distance in feet from group_in_reach, written at $B651 and printed two columns wide at the right of the line.

Is the group record at ($79) in reach of the current party? Carry set when it is on another map (byte 2 != $09), empty (byte 0, its column, is 0), farther than the reach $7D ($04CF, feet), outside the map view ($B119), beyond the distance in byte 0 of its square's record, or out of sight ($8347: a square of class 11 between). Otherwise carry clear, $77/$78 = the square's record (group_square_record) and A = the distance.
Operand of the LDX # at $B6B7: the group's map column (record byte 0), written at $B6A0; it goes to the view test $B119 and, reloaded at $B6CB, to the line-of-sight test $8347.
Operand of the LDY # at $B6B9: the group's map row (record byte 1), written at $B6A7; reloaded at $B6CE for $8347.
Operand of the CMP # at $B6C7: the group's distance in feet, written at $B6B0. Byte 0 of the square's record is compared with it (smaller: carry set, out of reach) and $B6D4 returns it in A.

Order W (Weapon) for member A: count_items ($033E) on the current character; with no items message 64 'You don't have anything.' and carry set; otherwise jumps to item_list_page ($0347) for member A, which returns the chosen slot with carry clear, or carry set.

Order H (Hire): reach $7D = $FF (any distance) and count_lines_in_reach; with none, message 57 'No one is within range.' and carry set; otherwise group_list_show and list_choose: carry clear with the chosen line index (0-47) in A after the line flashes; left-arrow returns carry set.

Order R (Run): in a party of more than one, message 36 'P)arty or S)ingle player?' (left-arrow cancels, other keys are ignored); then the map is drawn ($AC8C) and ask_direction asks 'Which way?'; the roster and picture window come back. Returns the direction 0-4 in A, ORed with $80 for P)arty; carry set when cancelled.

Order L (Load/unjam): carry clear (accepted) when the equipped weapon is jammed (count byte bit 7: the round tries to unjam it) or when the member carries its ammunition item (weapon record byte 7, find_item). Otherwise the window is cleared and message 66 'weapon can't be reloaded.' (no ammunition item) or 65 'has no more clips.' is printed with the (RETURN) prompt; carry set.
BIT $42A9 skips the LDA #$42 at $B75B when coming from $B758

Order U (Use) for member A: the Use dialog $8AD5; carry clear with A = its A * 16 + its X, and its Y stored at $5BDB + the member's record number; carry set when cancelled. The roster is shown again either way.
Operand of the ORA # at $B77C: the Use dialog's X result, written at $B776; it becomes the low nibble of the Use argument.
Operand of the LDY # at $B781: the member (1-7) choose_use works for, written on entry ($B76E); it indexes the party table at ($68) for the member's record number.

Slow CON changes of every character, records 1 to $0A in all parties: from $AF7B when a time step leaves the tick counter $D2 at a multiple of 16, and after each battle round ($B396). Dead records (CON 0) are skipped. On each call UNC characters recover a point and wake at half of +$26/+$27 (the CON before the blow, $A934), worse ones lose a point (dead below -50); healthy ones below MAXCON heal a point when $D2 AND $3F is 0 ($7F in the current party), and an affliction (+$28 bits 4-7) costs points when $D2 AND $3F is 0. Neither the recovery nor the healing happens while +$28 is non-zero (con_heal_one), so a character with one of bits 0-3 set stays UNC or keeps its CON.

Per record: select it ($0338); a dead record (CON exactly 0) is skipped; an affliction (+$28 bits 4-7) goes to $B816; a negative CON goes to $B7BA from -1 to -10, to $B83C below -10; a positive CON to $B7E9.
UNC (-1 to -10): one point back (con_heal_one, not while +$28 is non-zero); at 0 the character wakes with CON = (+$26/+$27) / 2, or 1 when that is 0.
Operand of the LDA # at $B7DD: the record health_tick is on (1 to $0A), written at $B797. 0 as loaded from disk; 4 in play-map, the last of that game's four characters.
Positive CON: below MAXCON (+$1B/+$1C) it heals a point (con_heal_one) when $D2 AND $3F is 0, or $D2 AND $7F for a character of the current party $08 (find_party_of, $02B1).
Afflicted (+$28 bits 4-7), when $D2 AND $3F is 0: a conscious character loses a point and at 0 drops to -1 (UNC); one who is not conscious goes to $B834.
Afflicted and not conscious: con_worsen, and once more unless that left CON at 0.
Below -10 (SER or worse): con_worsen, one point a tick.
Takes one more CON point (con_lose_one); when that leaves the low byte below $CE (CON below -50), CON becomes 0: the character dies.
Gives the current character one CON point ($0407 with X:A = -1) unless its status byte +$28 is non-zero.
Takes one CON point from the current character: $0407 with A = 1, X = 0 (16-bit subtract from +$1D/+$1E).

One battle round (from $B2A0, once the orders are confirmed): text window, message 30 'Encounter begins...' on row 13, slow scrolling on. Through $9F40 (each party on the battle map $8D, selected with $9C17): first $9F70, the members with the Attack order and a ranged reach ($9FA9); if any party was there, then $9C65, $7F64 and $9EFD (every member's order through the table $9F2E). Then $B8A6, slow scrolling off, the roster, and on into animation_on.
The round's actions are done: animation off, the run and party-move orders ($A276), then each party 0 to $0B selected ($9C17) and passed through $9959.
Operand of the LDA # at $B8B7: the party (0 to $0B) battle_round is finishing, written at $B8AE; each is selected with $9C17 and run through $9959.
Portrait animation on: $AC = 1 (the engine's animate_picture_tick does nothing while $AC is 0). The BIT at $B8CA hides animation_off's LDA #0.
BIT $00A9 skips animation_off's LDA #0
Portrait animation off: $AC = 0 (entered behind the BIT at $B8CA).

Asks 'Which way?' with the I / J space L / K diagram (message 68) at column 0, row 18 in the cleared message area, the window kept ($0247/$024C), and waits for one of direction_keys: A = 0 I, 1 K, 2 J, 3 L, 4 space, carry clear; left-arrow returns carry set. The portrait animation is off meanwhile and restored after.
Keys of ask_direction: I K J L space ($C9 $CB $CA $CC $A0), zero-terminated; the index is the direction 0-4.
Asks 'Use these options (Y/N)?' (message 70) and falls into ask_yes_no.
Waits for Y or N, ignoring other keys: Y returns carry clear; N or left-arrow carry set.

Picture for the encounter of party $08 (from orders_member_loop): with reach $7D = $FF and output off ($A1 = 1), nearest_line looks among the party's own 12 monster lines, then among all 48. The nearest line's monster name (its kind, messages 83-87, while the encounter is not identified: print_monster_name $9E5D) becomes the caption at $F4D0, centred on 11 characters, and its record's byte 7 the picture; with none in reach, 'Ranger' (message 96) and picture 8. Ends in show_picture ($0419).

A line was found: output back on, word-wrapped ($0302); the item becomes party, group and line; the monster's name goes into the line buffer ($9E5D) and its record's byte 7 is the picture ($9E9F, $9EDE).

Operand of the LDX # at $B960: nearest_line leaves the nearest item (line index + 1) here ($B9D2); encounter_portrait reads it at $B950 and rewrites it with that item's line (0-2) at $B958 for the monster record lookup $9E9F.

Caption: $F4D0-$F4DA filled with spaces and $F4DB = 0; the name in the line buffer ($F49D on, glyph + $20) is copied in from column 5 - length / 2 (0 for 11 characters or more) and cut at 11; then show_picture ($0419) with the picture number, whose window draw prints the caption at column 1, row 13 (engine $0571-$057D).

Finds the nearest monster line among A list items from item X+1: each goes through line_test, and of those in reach the one whose group's stored distance (byte 3, written by groups_measure and at $9416) is smallest wins, not the distance group_in_reach has just measured. Carry clear with the item in $B961 and line_test run on it again, leaving $77/$79 on it; carry set when none is in reach. $0253 counts the items.
Operand of the LDY # at $B9B2: the item nearest_line is testing, written at $B9AA. encounter_portrait borrows the byte ($B981, $B987) for half the caption's length.
Operand of the CMP # at $B9C8: the smallest stored group distance found so far, $FF for none (set at $B9A5, lowered at $B9CC); $B9BB reads it to see whether any line was found.
Runs group_list_line on item A (carry clear when the line is in reach and not empty), then puts the text cursor back at column 1.
Slow scrolling on: $A8 = 1 (the engine's newline pauses by the speed $0F while it is set). The BIT at $B9E5 hides slow_scroll_clear's LDA #0.
BIT $00A9 skips slow_scroll_clear's LDA #0
Slow scrolling off: $A8 = 0 (entered behind the BIT at $B9E5).
A = A * 64 (six ASL): a fire mode into bits 6-7 of an Attack argument.
A = A * 16 (four ASL): the Use dialog's first value into the high nibble.

After a battle round ($B2AC): for each party 0-3, its groups 0-3 on this map ($09) are written back to their squares (group_write_back); empty groups are passed over, and the first group found on another map stops the scan of that party.
Operand of the LDA # at $B9FC: the party (0-3) groups_write_back is on, written at $B9F4 and read at $BA0F and $BA1F.
Operand of the LDX # at $BA12: the group (0-3) groups_write_back is on, written at $B9F9 and read as data at $BA17.
Next party; a group on another map ($BA0D) also ends the party's groups.

Writes group X of party A back to its map square: each line's live monsters (non-zero hit points, $A83C) go into the square record's count byte (+4/+6/+8), a line with none also gets type 0. A wiped-out group changes the square by the record's pair at $0A/$0B and is cleared (group_clear), carry set; when $0A has bit 7 neither happens, and the group record stays as it is, carry set; see $BA80 for survivors.
Operand of the LDA # at $BA3B: the party group_write_back works on, written on entry ($BA2A) and read at $BA68 and $BA80.
Operand of the LDX # at $BA3D: the group group_write_back works on, written on entry ($BA2D) and read at $BA6B and $BA83.
Operand of the LDX # at $BA42: the line (0-2) being written back, written at $BA38 and read as data at $BA53 and $BA5B.
Operand of the ADC # at $BA4C: the group's total of live monsters, zeroed at $BA35, added up at $BA4E and tested at $BA63 (0: the group is wiped out).
A line with no live monster: its type byte (+3/+5/+7) is set to 0 too.
Survivors: the group record stays unless bit 1 of the square record's byte 9 is set ($9EF6), which clears it after every round; carry set when cleared.

Announces a group at distance A: each line with monsters on a line of its own (count and name, print_line_count_name), then ' appear(s) at ' (message 46, in the plural by the last count printed), the distance and ' feet.' (message 71, which ends with the (RETURN) prompt). From $9454.
Operand of the LDY # at $BA9F: the line (0-2) print_group_appears is on, set at $BA97 and stepped at $BAAC.
Operand of the LDA # at $BABD: the distance in feet print_group_appears was called with (A, written at $BA8F), printed after ' appear(s) at '.
Prints monster line A of the square record at ($77): the count right-aligned in two columns (also the plural count $38) and the name ($9E5D); carry set when the line is empty.
Operand of the LDX # at $BADD: the line print_line_count_name prints, written on entry ($BAC7), for the name ($9E5D).
Offsets in an encounter square's record of the monster counts of its lines 0-2: 4, 6, 8.
Offsets in an encounter square's record of the monster types of its lines 0-2: 3, 5, 7.
Measures every encounter group on the current map: for each party on map $09, each non-empty group's byte 3 = its distance in feet from that party ($04CF). Restores the current party.
Operand of the CMP # at $BAFE: the map ($09) groups_measure was called on, written at $BAEE; a party on another map is skipped.
Operand of the LDA # at $BB07: the party (0 to $0B) groups_measure is on, written at $BAF6.
Operand of the LDX # at $BB1E: the group (0-3) groups_measure is on, written at $BB04.
Sets the ten per-monster flag bytes (+$14 to +$1D) of the three lines of group X of the current party to 1.
BIT $00A9 skips group_flags_clear's LDA #0
Clears the ten per-monster flag bytes (+$14 to +$1D) of the three lines of group X of the current party.
Operand of the LDX # at $BB47: the group whose flags group_flags_set and group_flags_clear fill, written at $BB3A.
Operand of the LDA # at $BB4C: the value stored in the flags, 1 (group_flags_set) or 0 (group_flags_clear), written at $BB3D.
Operand of the LDY # at $BB57: the line (0-2) whose flags are being filled, written at $BB42.
Changes the square of the group at ($79) as the pair at offset A of its square's record says: $5F/$60 = $77/$78 (left there), then map_cell_change ($042E) with the group's column and row (bytes 0/1).
Points $77/$78 at the record of the square of the group at ($79) (bytes 0/1), keeping $5F/$60.
Points $77/$78 at the record of square X, Y ($042B, then $0428), keeping $5F/$60.
Points $77/$78 at entry A of the list of square class Y ($0428), keeping $5F/$60.
Points $79/$7A at line Y (0-2) of group X of party A: the group record + 4 + 30 * Y.
Operand of the LDY # at $BBB2: the line (0-2) group_line_ptr steps to, 30 bytes each, written on entry ($BB9F).
Points $79/$7A at group X (0-3) of party A (0-3): $EE00 + 376 * A + 94 * X.
Operand of the LDY # at $BBE7: the group (0-3) group_ptr steps to, 94 bytes each, written on entry ($BBC7).
Counts the monster lines in reach of member A (member_reach first).
Counts the monster lines in reach $7D across every group of parties 0 to $0B (group_in_reach and a non-zero count). Returns the count in A.
Operand of the LDA # at $BC0C: the party (0 to $0B) count_lines_in_reach is on, written at $BC04.
Operand of the LDX # at $BC25: the group (3 down to 0) count_lines_in_reach is on, written at $BC09.
Operand of the LDA # at $BC36: the number of monster lines in reach, zeroed at $BC01 and counted at $BC1F; count_lines_in_reach returns it in A.

Reach of member A, in feet: 0 when not conscious (then $7E is left as it was). Otherwise 15 (melee), or $FE for a weapon of a ranged class that has rounds in it and is not jammed (weapon_rounds puts an empty or jammed gun back to 15). Sets $7D = the reach and, for a conscious member, $7E = the weapon's class (1 for any weapon not of a ranged class); returns A = $7D.
Conscious: reach 15 (melee); a weapon of a ranged class (item_class $0365, $0413) gives $FE with $7E = its class, anything else $7E = 1; weapon_rounds then drops an empty or jammed gun back to 15.
Clears the group record at ($79): 94 bytes of zero.
Rounds in the current character's equipped weapon: weapon_use_rounds with 0, which also sets the reach $7D to 15 when the gun is empty or jammed.

Uses A rounds of the current character's equipped weapon and returns the rounds left (bits 0-5 of its count byte, never below 0). An empty or jammed gun sets the reach $7D to 15; a jammed one, or no weapon slot, returns 15; a weapon that is not ranged, or has no clip (record byte 4 = 0), returns 1. From the attack code ($A040, $A222).
Not a ranged weapon, or one without a clip (record byte 4 = 0): A = 1.

Gun with a clip: no weapon slot, or the jammed bit 7, gives reach 15 and A = 15 ($BCBB). Otherwise rounds (bits 0-5) minus the use: 0 or less stores 0 and sets reach 15; bits 6-7 kept. Returns the rounds left.
Operand of the ADC # at $BCA9: minus the number of rounds to use, written at $BC7A (0 through weapon_rounds).
Operand of the ORA # at $BCB4: bits 6-7 of the weapon's count byte, written at $BCA1 and put back with the new rounds.
Reach $7D = 15 (melee only); A = 15.
Points $89/$8A at the order table of party A ($F438 + 16 * A) and $8B/$8C eight bytes on, at its argument table.
Offsets of the four parties' order tables from $F438: 0, 16, 32, 48.
Shows one of two map messages at random: the message number at offset A+1 or A+2 of the current map's record ($61), through print_map_message ($0317).
Shows the map message whose number is at record offset Y of the current map ($61), through print_map_message.
A = A + 1 or A + 2, at random.
Operand of the ADC # at $BCF3: the A add_1_or_2 was called with, written at $BCEA.
Prints the names of the members flagged in $F3E5-$F3EB as 'A, B and C' (' and ' through $ABB6); nothing when none. From $A353, before ' move.' (message 92) when a party moves together.
Operand of the LDA # at $BD15: the names still to print, written at $BD0A and counted down at $BD10; at 1 the separator is ' and ' ($ABB6) instead of ', '.
Prints the name of the next flagged member, from the position at $BD2D, and leaves the position after it.
Operand of the LDY # at $BD2C: the position (0-7) print_next_flagged searches from; zeroed at $BCFA and left one past the member just printed ($BD36).

First the alphabet, 60 bytes: the character for each 5-bit code, codes 0-$1D directly; code $1E capitalises the next letter and code $1F reads one more code and takes entry $1E + it.
